classes.name: Dragonknight
classes.intro: Dragonknight is a class in Elder Scrolls Online. It is geared primarily towards tanking characters, but also utilizing fire to deal magic damage.
classes.desc: These skillful masters-at-arms use the ancient Akaviri martial arts tradition of battle-spirit, and wield fearsome magic that pounds, shatters and physically alters the world around them.

classes.name: Sorcerer
classes.intro: Sorcerer is a class in Elder Scrolls Online. Sorcerer is the class with the most magical abilities. It contains three skill lines, which each contain different types of spells for different roles. It is typically focused on lightning magic, similarly to the Dragonknight's emphasis on fire magic and Warden's use of ice magic.
classes.desc: Sorcerers can use conjuration and destruction spells to hurl lightning bolts and create shock fields, wield dark magic to snare and stun, and summon Daedric combat followers from Oblivion to assist them.

classes.name: Nightblade
classes.intro: Nightblade is a class in Elder Scrolls Online. Nightblade is tailored to benefit assassins and players who prefer a stealthy approach. There are three known skills governed by Nightblade: Assassination, Shadow, and Siphoning.
classes.desc: Nightblades are adventurers and opportunists with a gift for getting in and out of trouble. Relying variously on stealth, blades, and speed, Nightblades thrive on conflict and misfortune, trusting to their luck and cunning to survive.

classes.name: Templar
classes.intro: Templar is a class in Elder Scrolls Online. They wield the powers of light and the burning sun to smite the wicked, or to heal and support the wounded.
classes.desc: These traveling knights call upon the powers of light and the burning sun to deal massive damage to their enemies while restoring health, magicka, and stamina to their allies.

classes.name: Warden
classes.intro: Warden is a class in Elder Scrolls Online. It was originally only available to players who had purchased the Morrowind Chapter and later available as a separate Crown Store Upgrade for 1500 Crowns, but it has been integrated into the base game on March 9, 2026. Warden is a nature-themed class, with a focus on frost magic and animal companions.
classes.desc: Wardens are defenders of the Green, master storytellers whose nature tales become magical reality. They wield frost spells against enemies and summon animals to aid them.

classes.name: Necromancer
classes.intro: Necromancer is a class in Elder Scrolls Online. It can be purchased from the Crown Store for 1500 Crowns. Necromancers are death bringers who use a mix of Illusion, Destruction, and Conjuration spells, and mostly deal with the undead and fear. It is available to players who have purchased the retail version of the Elsweyr Chapter, but is not included with the DLC version of Elsweyr.
classes.desc: Masters of death, Necromancers can call upon corpses to serve as undead thralls and weave ghastly spells to both harm and heal.

classes.name: Arcanist
classes.desc: Channel the eldritch powers of Apocrypha as an Arcanist. These scholarly spellcasters channel secret runes and abyssal spells to destroy their enemies, heal their allies, and defend against any foe.

races.name: Argonian
races.desc: The racial skills of the Argonians reflect their people's perilous swamp environment; giving them bonuses to healing done, restoration staves, disease resistance, resources gained from consuming potions, swimming speed, as well as base health and magicka.

races.name: Breton
races.desc: The racial skills of the Bretons reflect their affinity for the arcane, increasing their base magicka, magicka recovery, light armor, alliance point gain, spell resistance, and cost reduction of spells, allowing them to cast spells with little pause.

races.name: Dark Elf
races.desc: The racial skills of the Dark Elves reflect their intellect and agility, giving them bonuses in dual wielding, flame and lava resistance, weapon and spell damage, and base magicka and stamina. These bonuses allow them to adapt to anything.

races.name: High Elf
races.desc: The racial skills of the High Elves reflect their magical affinity by increasing their spell damage, resource recovery, base magicka, and experience gain. These innate bonuses help define the race as proud and powerful spell casters.

races.name: Imperial
races.desc: The racial skills of the Imperials reflect their combat training and perseverance in battle, giving them bonuses to gold drop rates, shield proficiency, base health and stamina, and resource recovery when fighting back, making them resolute fighters.

races.name: Khajiit
races.desc: The racial skills of the feline Khajiit reflect their natural versatility and guile, giving them bonuses to pickpocketing, stealth, resource recovery, as well as base health, magicka, and stamina. These bonuses help them thrive in many ventures of life.

races.name: Nord
races.desc: The racial skills of the Nords reflect their strong and hardy natures, giving them bonuses to two-handed weapon use, duration of effects from drinks, physical, spell, and frost resistance, ultimate generation, as well as base health and stamina.

races.name: Orc
races.desc: The racial skills of the Orcs reflect their native harsh mountain environment, giving them bonuses to heavy armor use, sprinting, weapon damage, inspiration gain, weapon proficiency, as well as base health and stamina.

races.name: Redguard
races.desc: The racial skills of the Redguards reflect their ancestral legacy as sword masters, giving them bonuses to shields, base stamina, stamina recovery, movement, and duration of effects from food. Their ability to flow in martial combat is unparalleled.

races.name: Wood Elf
races.desc: The diversified racial skills of the Wood Elves reflect their woodland affinity. Improved archery, base stamina, stamina recovery, stealth detection, movement speed, reduced fall damage, and poison resistance make them dangerous foes and gifted hunters.

dual-wield.name: Dual Wield
dual-wield.intro: Dual Wield is one of the six weapon skills available in Elder Scrolls Online. You can advance through this skill line by equipping two One-Handed weapons.

aedric-spear.name: Aedric Spear
aedric-spear.intro: Aedric Spear is one of three class skill lines available to Templar characters. It can be learned by other classes via subclassing. Abilities in this line focus on melee weapon attacks.

dawns-wrath.name: Dawn's Wrath
dawns-wrath.intro: Dawn's Wrath is one of three class skill lines available to Templar characters. It can be learned by other classes via subclassing. Abilities in this line focus on magical attacks.

restoring-light.name: Restoring Light
restoring-light.intro: Restoring Light is one of three class skill lines available to Templar characters. It can be learned by other classes via subclassing. Abilities in this line focus on magical defense, support, and healing.

one-hand-and-shield.name: One Hand and Shield
one-hand-and-shield.intro: One Hand and Shield is one of the six weapon skills available in Elder Scrolls Online. Skills in this line focus on damage mitigation and various methods of stunning or controlling enemies. In addition, completing a fully charged heavy attack on an enemy will recharge the user's stamina based on their level. Use of these abilities, as well as progression through this skill line, requires equipping a one-handed weapon and a shield at the same time. Note that only equipping a shield will not train this skill, while still providing the benefit of the armor, trait and enchantment.

destruction-staff.name: Destruction Staff
destruction-staff.intro: Destruction Staff is one of the six weapon skills available in Elder Scrolls Online. You can advance through this skill line by equipping a Destruction type staff.

restoration-staff.name: Restoration Staff
restoration-staff.intro: Restoration Staff is one of the six weapon skills available in Elder Scrolls Online. Most active and passive abilities enabled by Restoration Staves focus on protecting and healing allies, while others help recharge the user's magicka. In addition, dealing a fully-charged heavy attack to an enemy will also recharge the user's magicka based on their level. The use of these abilities, and progression in the skill line, require equipping a Restoration type staff.

assassination.name: Assassination
assassination.intro: Assassination is one of three class skill lines available to Nightblades. It can be learned by other classes via subclassing. Abilities in this line focus on melee weapon attacks.

shadow.name: Shadow
shadow.intro: Shadow is one of three class skill lines available to Nightblades. It can be learned by other classes via subclassing. Abilities in this line focus on self-preservation through limiting enemies' attacks and hiding.

siphoning.name: Siphoning
siphoning.intro: Siphoning is one of three class skill lines available to Nightblades. It can be learned by other classes via subclassing. Abilities in this line focus on magicka attacks and debuffs.

ardent-flame.name: Ardent Flame
ardent-flame.intro: Ardent Flame is one of three class skill lines available to Dragonknights. It can be learned by other classes via subclassing. Abilities in this line focus on dealing fire damage.

draconic-power.name: Draconic Power
draconic-power.intro: Draconic Power is one of three class skill lines available to Dragonknights. It can be learned by other classes via subclassing. Abilities in this line focus on avoiding damage.

earthen-heart.name: Earthen Heart
earthen-heart.intro: Earthen Heart is one of three class skill lines available to Dragonknights. It can be learned by other classes via subclassing. Abilities in this line focus on utility, with stuns, effects, heals, and knock-backs.

storm-calling.name: Storm Calling
storm-calling.intro: Storm Calling is one of three class skill lines available to Sorcerer characters. It can be learned by other classes via subclassing. Abilities in this line focus on dealing magical damage.

daedric-summoning.name: Daedric Summoning
daedric-summoning.intro: Daedric Summoning is one of three class skill lines available to Sorcerer characters. It can be learned by other classes via subclassing. Abilities on this line call upon Daedric pacts and allies for strength.

dark-magic.name: Dark Magic
dark-magic.intro: Dark Magic is one of three class skill lines available to Sorcerer characters. It can be learned by other classes via subclassing. Abilities in this line focus on stuns and utility spells.

light-armor.name: Light Armor
light-armor.intro: Light Armor is a skill in Elder Scrolls Online. It consists largely of robes and cloth armor. As with the other armor skills, there are only passive skills and a single active ability. These skills mainly aid magic using characters.

medium-armor.name: Medium Armor
medium-armor.intro: Medium Armor is a skill in Elder Scrolls Online. It consists largely of leather, hide, and other low-weight armors. As with the other armor skills, there are only passive skills and a single active ability. These skills generally aid stamina-based characters.

heavy-armor.name: Heavy Armor
heavy-armor.intro: Heavy Armor is a skill in Elder Scrolls Online. It consists largely of plate armors. As with the other armor skills, there are only passive skills and a single active ability. These skills generally aid "tank" characters— those who require a lot of health.

soul-magic.name: Soul Magic
soul-magic.intro: Soul Magic is a skill line available to all players. The skill line and the Soul Trap ability (below) are unlocked from the start if you skip the tutorial. Otherwise, they will unlock when you complete Soul Shriven in Coldharbour at the start of the Main Quest. Soul Magic abilities center around acquiring and using souls from enemy creatures.

assault.name: Assault
assault.intro: Assault is one of the skill lines unlocked through progress in the Alliance War.

support.name: Support
support.intro: Support is one of the skill lines unlocked through progress in the Alliance War.

legerdemain.name: Legerdemain
legerdemain.intro: Legerdemain is a skill line available to all players. It becomes available once you successfully pickpocket an NPC, steal an item, pick a lock, or Fence/Launder stolen goods at an Outlaws Refuge. Legerdemain abilities focus on improving your ability to steal and fence items as part of the Justice System. The max level is 20.

green-balance.name: Green Balance
green-balance.intro: Green Balance is one of three class skill lines available to Wardens. It can be learned by other classes via subclassing. Abilities in this line focus on healing.

living-death.name: Living Death
living-death.intro: Living Death is one of three class skill lines available to Necromancers. It can be learned by other classes via subclassing. Abilities in this line focus on support and healing. Known abilities in this skill are listed below.

grave-lord.name: Grave Lord
grave-lord.intro: Grave Lord is one of three class skill lines available to Necromancers. It can be learned by other classes via subclassing. Abilities in this line focus on dealing damage. Known abilities in this skill are listed below.

bone-tyrant.name: Bone Tyrant
bone-tyrant.intro: Bone Tyrant is one of three class skill lines available to Necromancers. It can be learned by other classes via subclassing. Abilities in this line focus on defense and tanking. Known abilities in this skill are listed below.

auriels-bow.name: Auriel's Bow
auriels-bow.intro: Auriel's Bow is an artifact associated with the Elven God Auriel, and is an artifact to potentially be released in the future. Sheogorath unleashed the various artifacts upon Cyrodiil for the purpose of putting an end to his boredom surrounding the lack of chaos in the Three Banners War, and for the fun of keeping his Daedric siblings on their guard.

sanguines-rose.name: Sanguine's Rose
sanguines-rose.intro: Sanguine's Rose is an artifact associated with the Daedric Prince Sanguine and is an artifact to potentially be released in the future. Sheogorath unleashed the various artifacts upon Cyrodiil for the purpose of putting an end to his boredom surrounding the lack of chaos in the Three Banners War, and for the fun of keeping his Daedric siblings on their guard.

herald-of-the-tome.name: Herald of the Tome
herald-of-the-tome.intro: Herald of the Tome is one of three class skill lines available to Arcanists. It can be learned by other classes via subclassing. Abilities in this line focus on dealing damage.

soldier-of-apocrypha.name: Soldier of Apocrypha
soldier-of-apocrypha.intro: Soldier of Apocrypha is one of three class skill lines available to Arcanists. It can be learned by other classes via subclassing. Abilities in this line focus on defense and tanking.

curative-runeforms.name: Curative Runeforms
curative-runeforms.intro: Curative Runeforms is one of three class skill lines available to Arcanists. It can be learned by other classes via subclassing. Abilities in this line focus on healing and support.

class-mastery.name: Class Mastery
class-mastery.intro: Class Mastery is a skill system introduced with Update 50 that provides passive skill lines for each of the seven Player Classes. Each class will have five different passive skills and for each character you will be able to pick two of them.

two-handed.name: Two Handed
two-handed.intro: Two Handed is one of the six weapon skills available in Elder Scrolls Online. You can advance through this skill line by equipping a two-handed weapon.

winters-embrace.name: Winter's Embrace
winters-embrace.intro: Winter's Embrace is one of three class skill lines available to Wardens. It can be learned by other classes via subclassing. Abilities in this line focus on dealing frost damage, and shielding you and your group from damage.

volendrung.name: Volendrung
volendrung.intro: Volendrung is an artifact associated with the Daedric Prince Malacath, stolen by Sheogorath to keep the other Princes on their toes and bring more chaos to the Three Banners War. It was added into the game with the release of the Elsweyr chapter. For more information on the backstory behind Volendrung, see the lore article.

places.name: Aetherian Archive
places.desc: a tower in southeastern Craglorn near the city of Elinhir.
places.loadtext: For untold ages this tower has loomed over Elinhir, its portals mystically sealed, all entry forbidden. Someone exerted immense effort to place impenetrable wards on this place—but now those wards are sundered.

places.name: Arx Corinium
places.desc: a group dungeon found in southwestern Shadowfen.
places.loadtext: The Second Empire made some advances into the periphery of Black Marsh, but they didn't stay long. Arx Corinium, once an Imperial fort, is now occupied by denizens of the deep swamp—and even stranger things.

places.name: Asylum Sanctorium
places.desc: a mini trial found within the Reactor District in the Brass Fortress.
places.loadtext: Sotha Sil is rumored to have been the one to reverse engineer the Soul Gems in order to create Black Soul Gems. When he began this process, he used three Dunmer Saints for experiments to see if he could grant everlasting life. Three mechanical creations were made to house the souls of these saints.

places.name: Bal Sunnar
places.desc: a group dungeon in Stonefalls.
places.loadtext: "They came for us once, and I believe they will return. No one can say when—their arrival is always unannounced. Our captors call them 'Scourge,' but we know them as saviors." —Biwulm, servant at Bal Sunnar

places.name: Bedlam Veil
places.desc: a demiplane and group dungeon accessed from a portal in Wrothgar.
places.loadtext: Filled with powerful weapons and objects of fame, the Bedlam Veil is the trophy house of Fa-Nuit-Hen. Very few visiting warriors are given access to the veil, though the ones that do describe it as a triumph of martial curation.

places.name: Black Drake Villa
places.desc: a group dungeon on the Gold Coast.
places.loadtext: After the fall of the Longhouse Emperors, this grand retreat stayed largely abandoned aside from the occasional treasure hunter. Most of the spoils of Durcorach's campaign across Tamriel went missing, only to appear later on the black market.

places.name: Black Gem Foundry
places.desc: a mining facility and group dungeon in Coldharbour accessed from southern Solstice.
places.loadtext: "The reapers sustain the Writhing Wall. But the weapons and armor forged in our foundry will outfit those that guard it and ensure that no soul escapes bondage, no essence goes unclaimed by our Lord of Domination." —High Soulbinder Vykand

places.name: Blackheart Haven
places.desc: a group dungeon found in Bangkorai.
places.loadtext: The Bjoulsae River, where it widens as it enters the Iliac Bay, flows past dozens of small islands that have long served as refuges for smugglers and sea raiders. The most notorious of these hideouts is Blackheart Haven.

places.name: Blackrose Prison
places.desc: a group-based arena in Murkmire, located southeast of Dead-Water Village.
places.loadtext: When Imperial Potentate Versidue-Shaie wanted a distant dungeon to house the most feared criminal and political prisoners of the Second Empire, he ordered a penal institution built on the coast of Black Marsh; it was named Blackrose Prison after the ancient city a day's march to the north.

places.name: Blessed Crucible
places.desc: a group dungeon found in the Rift.
places.loadtext: Warriors from all over Tamriel whisper about the Blessed Crucible, the hidden arena in the mountains of Skyrim where the mighty contend for fame, wealth, and the fabled Brimstone Crown.

places.name: Bloodroot Forge
places.desc: a group dungeon in Craglorn.
places.loadtext: Shunned by the Nords as a place of evil, this mystic forge site was constructed by an unknown Nedic sect that worshiped forgotten dark gods. Now it's been reopened by the Dreadhorn clan of Reachmen, who are meddling with dangerous forces of great power.

places.name: Castle Thorn
places.desc: a group dungeon nestled in the Haafingar Mountains of Western Skyrim.
places.loadtext: "Despite Lady Thorn's mysterious past, the Ravenwatch never felt the need to deal with her directly. She seemed content to hide away in the mountains, alone in her horrific castle. This one wonders if ignoring her was a terrible mistake." —Adusa-daro

places.name: City of Ash I
places.desc: a group dungeon found in Greenshade.
places.loadtext: Not all Wood Elves are happy about Valenwood joining the Aldmeri Dominion. Some fear for their beloved forests, while others fear their heritage and traditions will be diluted or replaced. A few groups have retreated to refuges deep in the jungle.

places.name: City of Ash II
places.desc: a group dungeon found in Greenshade.
places.loadtext: Nature has returned to reclaim the City of Ash. An unsealed portal still threatens, and only a few remain to defend against it.

places.name: Cloudrest
places.desc: a city found on the mountain of Eton Nir in Summerset, east of Ebon Stadmont.
bosses: Shade of Galenwe and Shade of Falarielle
Shade of Relequen and Shade of Belanaril
Shade of Siroria and Shade of Silaeda
places.loadtext: The Aerie of the Altmer, the city of Cloudrest clings to the highest slopes of the peak of Eton Nir, the tallest mountain on Summerset Isle. Somehow, its thin air is as heady and bracing as chilled nirnroot wine.

places.name: Coral Aerie
places.desc: an islet located off the northern coast of Summerset, accessed by taking a boat on the beach north of the Veyond Wyte Wayshrine.
places.loadtext: "This undisturbed little islet far off the coast of Summerset sports high cliffs and deep tide pools that act as popular breeding grounds for all manner of sea life, migratory birds, and even large predators. I recommend all nature watching be done from the safety of the ship."—Captain Marrisa

places.name: Cradle of Shadows
places.desc: a group dungeon in Shadowfen.
places.loadtext: The Cradle of Shadows is the seat of power of the enigmatic figure known only as the Lady of Lace. What lies behind its veil of darkness is known only by her fanatical followers.

places.name: Crypt of Hearts I
places.desc: a group dungeon found in Rivenspire.
places.loadtext: This place's forbidding black towers are visible for leagues, even through Rivenspire's drifting mists. Yet the local inhabitants never mention it, behaving as if it doesn't even exist. But the Crypt of Hearts is no illusion or mirage—it is solid and all too real.

places.name: Crypt of Hearts II
places.desc: a group dungeon found in Rivenspire.
places.loadtext: This place's forbidding black towers are visible for leagues, even through Rivenspire's drifting mists. Yet the local inhabitants never mention it, behaving as if it doesn't even exist. But the Crypt of Hearts is no illusion or mirage—it is solid and all too real.

places.name: Darkshade Caverns I
places.desc: a group dungeon found in southeastern Deshaan.
places.loadtext: These caves have the distinction of being the most famous kwama mines in Deshaan. Dark Elves consider kwama eggs a delicacy, and those harvested from Darkshade Caverns are particularly prized by Dunmeri gourmets.

places.name: Darkshade Caverns II
places.desc: a group dungeon found in southeastern Deshaan.
places.loadtext: These caves have the distinction of being the most famous kwama mines in Deshaan. Dark Elves consider kwama eggs a delicacy, and those harvested from Darkshade Caverns are particularly prized by Dunmeri gourmets.

places.name: Depths of Malatar
places.desc: a group dungeon on the Gold Coast.
places.loadtext: "The light that shone from the statue of Narilmor acted as both guide and protector to Ayleid ships crossing the Abecean, promising warmth and safe harbor in Garlas Malatar, until the city fell in the latter days of the Alessian Slave Rebellion." - Tjurhane Fyrre

places.name: Direfrost Keep
places.desc: a group dungeon found in Eastmarch.
places.loadtext: Ancestral home of the Direfrost clan, this frozen castle has long been sealed to the outside world, its owners neither seen nor heard from in generations. Mountain storms rage above the castle walls, conjured up by some unknown malignant power.

places.name: Dragonstar Arena
places.desc: a group-based arena in Upper Craglorn.
places.loadtext: Only the strongest and bravest warriors dare to face the challenges of the Dragonstar Arena.

places.name: Dreadsail Reef
places.desc: a reef off the coast of High Isle that serves as a major base for the Dreadsails, a group of Maormer pirates.
places.loadtext: Surrounded by jagged, shallow reefs and inhabited by fierce predators, this small islet on the far fringes of the Systres Archipelago was practically untouched by man or mer until the Dreadsail's Fleet Queen claimed it as her own.

places.name: Earthen Root Enclave
places.desc: an islet located off the southeast coast of High Isle, reached from a ship west of the Coral Road Wayshrine.
places.loadtext: "Earthen Root Enclave welcomes all druids who wish to commune with the Spirits of Stone, Root, and Air. Come, reconnect with Y'ffre in peace."—Archdruid Sonele

places.name: Elden Hollow I
places.desc: a group dungeon found under Elden Root in central Grahtwood.
places.loadtext: When the Daedra-worshiping Ayleids were driven from Cyrodiil after Alessia's Slave Rebellion, many of the Wild Elf clans took refuge in Valenwood. One of the foremost of those clans was granted the right to excavate dwelling-halls under Elden Root itself.

places.name: Elden Hollow II
places.desc: a group dungeon found under Elden Root in central Grahtwood.
places.loadtext: When the Daedra-worshiping Ayleids were driven from Cyrodiil after Alessia's Slave Rebellion, many of the Wild Elf clans took refuge in Valenwood. One of the foremost of those clans was granted the right to excavate dwelling-halls under Elden Root itself.

places.name: Exiled Redoubt
places.desc: a group dungeon in the northern mountains of the West Weald.
places.loadtext: "This is our fortress. This is where the dreams lost to death will be realized and forces that seem immutable will crumble. This exile may be of our own making, but it is through isolation that we change the course of a war." —Cato Albus, Patriarch

places.name: Falkreath Hold
places.desc: a group dungeon in Craglorn.
places.loadtext: Since Hakkvild drove out the Orcs in 2E 467 Falkreath has been back in the hands of the Nords. But now the weakened hold is menaced by another threat: the savage Reachmen of the Dreadhorn clan.

places.name: Fang Lair
places.desc: a group dungeon in Bangkorai.
places.loadtext: The Dwarven city of Arkngthamz-Phng rivaled the splendor of Dumac's kingdom before it was laid to waste by a Dragon in the First Era. The legend of that terrifying creature has long kept travelers far from Fang Lair ... until now.

places.name: Frostvault
places.desc: a group dungeon in northern Eastmarch.
places.loadtext: "Mhuvnak was known as one of the most gifted builders of architecture in Dwemereth, greatly expanding their underground kingdom with ingenious constructs until his disappearance on an expedition deep into Nord lands." —Guylaine Marilie

places.name: Fungal Grotto I
places.desc: a group dungeon located northwest of Iliath Temple.
places.loadtext: These extensive caverns in the volcanic rock beneath Stonefalls were once used for unknown purposes by the ancient Chimer, but were abandoned by the Elves long ago. Now they are the haunt of Goblins and other denizens of the underworld.

places.name: Fungal Grotto II
places.desc: a group dungeon located northwest of Iliath Temple
places.loadtext: These extensive caverns in the volcanic rock beneath Stonefalls were once used for unknown purposes by the ancient Chimer, but were abandoned by the Elves long ago. Now they are the haunt of Goblins and other denizens of the underworld.

places.name: Graven Deep
places.desc: a region located off the southwest coast of High Isle, accessed by ship from Amenos Station.
places.loadtext: "Yes, yes. This one has heard your besotted whispers about the mysterious Graven Deep. Samaril believes none of them. He has a shipment of Alik'r spice to deliver and a pack of cowardly sailors won't slow him down."—The final recorded words of Samaril, captain of the Azure Spirit.

places.name: Halls of Fabrication
places.desc: a part of Sotha Sil's Clockwork City.
places.loadtext: It is said that Sotha Sil's Fabrication Chambers can analyze anything in the Mundus, organic or inorganic, and reproduce it in clockwork form.
places.base_note: available for free since April 2022, and fully integrated into the base game since March 2026

places.name: Hel Ra Citadel
places.desc: an ancient Yokudan fortress in southwestern Craglorn.
places.loadtext: When the warriors of the Ra Gada came to the shores of Hammerfell, some of the fiercest cohorts marched far inland in search of domains to claim. Hel Ra was one of the easternmost of these domains, but its gates were sealed long ago.

places.name: Icereach
places.desc: a group dungeon on an island in the Sea of Ghosts, accessed by boat from Wrothgar's northern shore.
places.loadtext: Hidden among the churning waves of the Sea of Ghosts, this frigid isle serves as the seat of power for the cruel Icereach Coven. Now, lashing storms swirl around it. Could this be a natural phenomenon, or something more sinister?

places.name: Imperial City Prison
places.desc: a group dungeon found northeast of the Imperial City's Memorial District.
places.loadtext: This external district of the Imperial City houses the headquarters of the Imperial Legions, as well as the Imperial Prison itself. The City sewers pass beneath the prison as they drain toward Lake Rumare—but they're inaccessible, of course.
places.base_note: available for free since September 2019, and fully integrated into the base game with the launch of Update 49 on 6 March 2026

places.name: Infinite Archive
places.desc: a two-person arena located in a demiplane linked to Apocrypha.
places.loadtext: "What is life but a constant fight against unending enemies and unseen puppet masters across an ever-changing landscape? The Infinite Archive is not the exception to the struggles of existence, it is the quintessence of it."—Master Malkhest

places.name: Kyne's Aegis
places.desc: a bastion in the Sea of Ghosts, located on an island off the coast north of Solitude.
places.loadtext: While many Nords attribute the founding of Kyne's Aegis to Fuldimar Hookhand in , Dragon Cult ruins tell a far older—and darker—story.
places.base_note: integrated to the base game with the launch of Season Two on 21 October 2026

places.name: Lair of Maarselok
places.desc: a group dungeon within the mountain valleys of Tenmar, Grahtwood entered from a lake northeast of the Ossuary of Telacar.
places.loadtext: The fertile jungles of this mountain valley have long since swallowed up the Khajiit kingdom that once called it home. But a new, malignant growth is spreading here, and it threatens to consume far more than old ruins.

places.name: Lep Seclusa
places.desc: a group dungeon hidden on an island in the bay of Hew's Bane.
places.loadtext: "Caution? That's your advice? It's a small island filled with blind priests and warrior monks so focused on remaining hidden that they haven't fought anyone in living memory. How much trouble could they be?"—Orpheon the Tactician

places.name: Lucent Citadel
places.desc: a ruined stronghold in the wastelands of Fargrave, accessible from West Weald.
places.loadtext: Though shrouded in mystery, the Lucent Citadel stands as a gleaming structure in the sand of Fargrave's wastelands. Records and tales differ on the nature of what lies within, but all agree that the arcane knot must be powerful enough to make another expedition of brave explorers take the risk.

places.name: Maelstrom Arena
places.desc: an otherworldly solo arena accessed from Wrothgar.
places.loadtext: Untold thousands have tested their mettle against Maelstrom Arena―and failed.
places.base_note: free as a March 2024 daily login reward and fully integrated into the base game since March 2026

places.name: March of Sacrifices
places.desc: A dungeon shaped around the theme of Hircine's Great Hunt.
places.loadtext: For an Oblivion realm, Lord Hircine's plane of The Hunting Grounds, a vast wilderness of forest, meadow, and mountain, is almost familiar to those Tamrielic mortals who find their way there. Almost familiar, but not quite.
places.base_note: integrated into the base game with the launch of Season Two on 21 October 2026

places.name: Maw of Lorkhaj
places.desc: a desecrated Khajiiti temple in Reaper's March.
places.loadtext: An ancient Khajiiti shrine called the "Temple of Seven Riddles" has been overrun by the Khajiit's eternal enemy, the dro-m'Athra. With each passing hour, more Lost Cats pour into Nirn through a gaping rift between worlds. If Tamriel is to be saved, this Maw of Lorkhaj must be closed.
places.base_note: integrated into the base game since March 2026

places.name: Moon Hunter Keep
places.desc: A group dungeon located in Reaper's March, in a Colovian fort overrun by werewolves.
places.loadtext: Moon Hunter Keep! A name spoken by the Silver Dawn werewolf hunters of Reaper's March only in whispers—that is, when there still were Silver Dawn werewolf hunters in Reaper's March.
places.base_note: integrated into the base game with the launch of Season Two on 21 October 2026

places.name: Moongrave Fane
places.desc: a group dungeon in the ancient ruins of a forgotten Khajiiti faith.
places.loadtext: "Just as the sixteen kingdoms were not always one, so too were the faiths of the Khajiit many-fold. In guiding Khajiit along his one true path of the moons, Riddle'Thar hid from us all the others. But if you are wise, you may catch glimpses of where the walkers of old have tread." — Tsramusa the Exile

places.name: Naj-Caldeesh
places.desc: an ancient xanmeer and group dungeon built into a mountain west of Sunport.
places.loadtext: The only time Stone-Nest Argonians mention Naj-Caldeesh is around campfires. Whatever lurks within the lost xanmeer promises to be a daring adventure or terrifying end for whoever discovers the entrance.

places.name: Oathsworn Pit
places.desc: a group dungeon in the northern mountains of the Reach.
places.loadtext: As followers of Malacath, the Oathsworn are some of the most fearsome warriors in Tamriel. They're masters at multiple forms of combat and use the fiery heart of their sacred home to light their forges.

places.name: Opulent Ordeal
places.desc: a trial created by the enigmatic Opulent entities of the Night Market to test newcomers.
places.loadtext: The opulent look down over the rest of the Night Market with glee. They laugh at the poor attempts to understand the districts when they unlocked the secret long ago. Now they stand, waiting for anyone who can overcome a fraction of their power.

places.name: Ossein Cage
places.desc: a Coldharbour prison that is accessible from Solstice.
places.loadtext: The Ossein Cage stands as a testament to Coldharbour's cruel creativity. Accounts of the graveyard's tormented skeletal adornments serve as a warning to all and as a horrid promise to an unfortunate few.

places.name: Red Petal Bastion
places.desc: a group dungeon in northeast Glenumbra.
places.loadtext: Red Petal Bastion was not the first seat of power for the Knights of the Silver Rose, but it was built to be the last. Secured with all the defenses a kingdom's treasury could buy, the bastion ensures that the spoils of the order's many anti-Daedra crusades remain safely in the Silver Rose's hands.

places.name: Rockgrove
places.desc: an Argonian settlement and trial located in the southeastern reaches of Blackwood.
places.loadtext: Stone-talkers from the Ca-Uxith tribe have watched over Rockgrove's xanmeer for centuries. Although the stone stays silent, the chaos roiling beneath it could erupt at any moment. Before this occurs, a stone-talker will see the signs and prepare the tribe's defenses.

places.name: Ruins of Mazzatun
places.desc: a group dungeon in Shadowfen.
places.loadtext: As any Argonian will tell you, something at the heart of the "Puzzle City" is terribly wrong and deeply disturbing at a basic, almost organic level. Erect the spines of warning!

places.name: Sanctum Ophidia
places.desc: an ancient Nedic temple in northern Craglorn.
places.loadtext: The Sanctum caverns are works of art, carved masterpieces sealed long ago. Unfortunately for Craglorn, the Ophidians were always the most … fervent of the Celestial sects.

places.name: Sanity's Edge
places.desc: the dreamworld of Warlock Vanton.
places.loadtext: "A source of all hopes, dreams, and fears, the mind is an ever-changing landscape. It is our greatest asset, ally, and enemy all at once. Pray that yours never turns on you."—Wizard Twelvane

places.name: Scalecaller Peak
places.desc: A group dungeon located in Stormhaven.
places.loadtext: Abandoned by its Dragon Lord long ago, the temple of Zaan the Scalecaller remained empty for centuries, cold and discarded. Now a new cult has taken over the mountain, and their repugnant schemes threaten all of Tamriel.

places.name: Scrivener's Hall
places.desc: a group dungeon in the Rift.
places.loadtext: "It's easy to get lost in this maze of bookshelves and side rooms warped by contact with the unstable rifts into Oblivion. But the Scribes of Mora manage to find their way around due to their eons of cartographic experience."

places.name: Selene's Web
places.desc: a group dungeon found in Reaper's March.
places.loadtext: Even by the standards of , something is not right about the growth of the forest in this vicinity. It doesn't seem unhealthy—on the contrary, it seems vigorous, but in an unwholesome way.

places.name: Shipwright's Regret
places.desc: a shipyard located in eastern Rivenspire, east of Fell's Run.
places.loadtext: Baron-Admiral Bendu Olo was said to have spared no expense preparing his motley fleet for the war against the Sload. Some scholars claim he fully employed as much as three-fourths of Tamriel's shipbuilders while outfitting the All Flags Navy to brave the treacherous waters surrounding Thras.

places.name: Spindleclutch I
places.desc: a group dungeon found in northern Glenumbra.
places.loadtext: The Ayleid ruins of Dwynnarth that grin down from the bluffs above Hag Fen were plundered and emptied out generations ago. But it seems there are forgotten mine tunnels beneath the lowest levels of Dwynnarth that might not be quite so empty.

places.name: Spindleclutch II
places.desc: a group dungeon found in northern Glenumbra.
places.loadtext: The Ayleid ruins of Dwynnarth that grin down from the bluffs above Hag Fen were plundered and emptied out generations ago. But it seems there are forgotten mine tunnels beneath the lowest levels of Dwynnarth that might not be quite so empty.

places.name: Stone Garden
places.desc: a group dungeon found in the Greymoor Cavern section of Blackreach: Greymoor Caverns.
places.loadtext: "Dwarven pipes can transport more than just steam. Water, oil, air, even molten rock in some cases. That's the beauty of Dwemer designs. Their versatility means they can be repurposed for any use. It doesn't take a genius to see that, but it helps." —Raynor Vanos

places.name: Sunspire
places.desc: an ancient temple of Alkosh found in Northern Elsweyr.
places.loadtext: Before Rawl'kha Temple rose to prominence after the Riddle'Thar Epiphany, Sunspire was the preeminent house of worship in Anequina. If the rumors of Alkosh's return are true, it may be so again.

places.name: Tempest Island
places.desc: a small island containing a group dungeon accessible from Malabal Tor.
places.loadtext: Surrounded by sand bars and shifting channels, this island in the Strid estuary has long been a haven for pirates, raiders, and fugitives from law enforcement. It has never been fully explored by any civilized authority.

places.name: The Banished Cells I
places.desc: a group dungeon found at the northern tip of Auridon.
places.loadtext: The High Elves live long lives and have a talent for magic. Sometimes an Altmer's pursuit of magical power leads to tampering with forbidden knowledge and illicit dealings with evil Daedra. It was to confine such trespassers that the Banished Cells were created.

places.name: The Banished Cells II
places.desc: a group dungeon found at the northern tip of Auridon.
places.loadtext: The High Elves live long lives and have a talent for magic. Sometimes an Altmer's pursuit of magical power leads to tampering with forbidden knowledge and illicit dealings with evil Daedra. It was to confine such trespassers that the Banished Cells were created.

places.name: The Cauldron
places.desc: a group dungeon in western Deshaan.
places.loadtext: Once a thriving source of profit for the merchant Felisa Vendu, she abandoned this old mine after workers revolted. They insisted that voices came to them from the darkness. A low whispered chanting that followed them to their sleep, driving many of them mad. Since then, only fools have entered.

places.name: The Dread Cellar
places.desc: a group dungeon in northern Blackwood.
places.loadtext: "There is no place in Tamriel I'd have rather seen that curdled, sump wizard, Mannimarco, condemned to than the Dread Cellar. While its hospitality might not be the equal to that of Molag Bal's realm, it's a damnable pit I have visitation privileges to."—Abnur Tharn

places.name: Unhallowed Grave
places.desc: a tomb complex and group dungeon located in the desert wastes of Bangkorai.
places.loadtext: Long ago, the soldiers of the Bangkorai Garrison buried something away in this accursed cavern—an evil too great to leave unguarded. Now, centuries later, even the most daring Redguard explorers know to give this grave a wide berth.

places.name: Vateshran Hollows
places.desc: a solo arena in the Reach, south of the Reachwind Ritual Site.
places.loadtext: "Try not to cross paths with members of the Spiritblood clan. They show a brutality in battle that even scares other Reachfolk. Whether a gift of their blood or their style of combat training, their warriors do not cease until they lay dead."—Valencia Pitio, Imperial Commandant
places.base_note: added to the base game on 9 November 2026

places.name: Vaults of Madness
places.desc: a group dungeon found in Coldharbour.
places.loadtext: The Vaults of Madness are the masterpiece of the infamous Mad Architect, who is said to be one of the few entities ever to serve multiple Daedric Princes and profit from it. How he is paid for his "services" is a matter of wild and horrible conjecture.

places.name: Volenfell
places.desc: a group dungeon found in Alik'r Desert.
places.loadtext: The ancient Dwarven city of Volenfell was long lost to the sands of the Alik'r Desert. But its ruins have recently been discovered, prompting a race between scholars and treasure-hunters to be the first to search its storied depths.

places.name: Wayrest Sewers I
places.desc: a group dungeon found under the city of Wayrest in Stormhaven.
places.loadtext: Wayrest is justifiably proud of the commodious modern sewers that drain the city's wastes into the Iliac Bay. But the curving conduits beneath the streets contain dark secrets unsuspected by those who walk in the light of day above.

places.name: Wayrest Sewers II
places.desc: a group dungeon found under the city of Wayrest in Stormhaven.
places.loadtext: Wayrest is justifiably proud of the commodious modern sewers that drain the city's wastes into the Iliac Bay. But the curving conduits beneath the streets contain dark secrets unsuspected by those who walk in the light of day above.

places.name: White-Gold Tower
places.desc: a group dungeon found in the center of the Imperial City.
places.loadtext: Built by the Ayleids as a focus of mystic power at the heart of Tamriel, the White-Gold Tower has long been a symbol of the Empires of Cyrodiil that followed. Now it is in danger of being absorbed into Coldharbour—and could draw Tamriel in after it!
places.base_note: available for free since September 2019, and fully integrated into the base game with the launch of Update 49 on 6 March 2026

sections.title: How to come back after a break
sections.answer: Take the Path to Adventure if it is offered, claim the zones that joined the base game, rebuild your character for free, then pick up the new seasonal systems.
sections.need: You'll need: one level 50 character for subclassing and Class Mastery.

steps.t: If the short Path to Adventure mini-quest appears when you log in, accept it.
steps.q: For returning players, they’ll see it first thing on their next log-in and be offered the short mini-quest that will help them rediscover combat basics.

steps.t: Open the **Collections** menu to see which content your account now owns.
steps.q: As a reminder, to see what content is owned on your account, visit the Collections Menu and visit the Collectibles, Stories, etc. tabs.

steps.t: Log in once to receive Markarth, which joined the base game with Update 51 Incremental 2.
steps.q: Players who do not own this DLC will receive it upon their first login after Update 51 Incremental 2 is live.

steps.t: Visit [[Western Skyrim]] and [[The Reach]]: Greymoor and Markarth are now free with the base game.
steps.q: Venture into Skyrim's dark heart with both Greymoor and Markarth becoming free with ESO's base game.

steps.t: Reallocate your skill points from the **Skills** screen; since Update 49 this costs nothing.
steps.q: As of Update 49, spent skill points can be reallocated directly from the Skills screen at no cost.

steps.t: Get the free Armory Station from the Crown Store.
steps.q: An Armory Station collectible furnishing is available for free from the Crown Store and can be placed in player houses to access the system.

steps.t: Save your build at the Armory Station so you can swap attributes, skills, gear, Champion Points and outfits later.
steps.q: This allows you to quickly change your attributes, skills, equipment, Champion Points, and Outfits.

steps.t: Train your Riding Skill at a stable once per day.
steps.q: Your Riding Skill is character-bound and can only be improved once a day at a stable.

steps.t: Decide between subclassing (added in Update 46) and [[Class Mastery]] (added in Update 50).
q: Subclassing is a system that was released in the base game Update 46.
Class Mastery: This new feature grants access to powerful passive effects for characters that have reached level 50 in their native class skill lines and are not actively subclassing.

steps.t: Complete Weekly and Seasonal challenges to progress the current Tamriel Tome.
steps.q: Progression through a Tome is done by completing Weekly and Seasonal challenges.

steps.t: Open the **Group & Activity Finder** to join the active Golden Pursuit.
steps.q: They are dynamic, one-off campaigns (accessed from the Group & Activity Finder) that allow you to earn additional rewards during special limited-time windows.

steps.t: If you used [[The Apprentice]] for spell damage, switch to [[The Warrior]] in [[Malabal Tor]], [[Alik'r Desert]], [[Eastmarch]] or [[Cyrodiil]].
q: The Apprentice now grants an 8% bonus to experience and inspiration gain, rather than Spell Damage.
If you previously used this stone for the spell damage bonus and would like to swap to the Warrior, that stone can be found in Malabal Tor, the Alik’r Desert, Eastmarch, or in Cyrodiil.

sections.check: Your Collections show Greymoor and Markarth as owned, and your Armory holds a saved build.

more.t: Season Two: Echoes of Skyrim runs from October 21, 2026 until January 27, 2027.
more.q: Released on October 21, 2026 and runs until January 27, 2027.

more.t: Tamriel Tomes replaced the old Endeavor and Daily Login Reward systems in March 2026.
more.q: Tomes incorporated the previous Endeavor and Daily Login Reward systems, which were disabled in March 2026.

more.t: The free Tome is open to all players; the paid Premium Tome unlocks premium rewards.
q: All Elder Scrolls Online players will have access to the free version of the tome
When purchased, it unlocks the premium rewards for a tome.

more.t: Up to 5,000 Tome Points roll over at the end of each Season.
more.q: Updated the Tamriel Tomes Overview Help menu entry to clarify that up to 5,000 Tome Points roll over at the end of each Season.

more.t: Path to Adventure is offered to returning players who have not earned the Level 20 Accountwide Achievement.
more.q: as well as returning players who have not acquired the Level 20 Accountwide Achievement.

more.t: Try the new solo versions of [[March of Sacrifices]] and [[Moon Hunter Keep]], entered from the world map or their entrances.
q: The March of Sacrifices and Moonhunter Keep dungeons now can be played in solo mode!
You can enter the solo version of these dungeons from the world map or their entrance in their corresponding zones.

more.t: The [[Warden]] class is part of the base game since Update 49.
more.q: The Warden class was added to the base game with the launch of Update 49 on 6 March 2026

more.t: Since Update 50 a character can complete up to 100 daily quests per day.
more.q: We have increased the cap on the number of daily quests that can be completed on a character per day from 50 to 100.

sections.title: How to level from 1 to 50
sections.answer: Quest, run dungeons through the Dungeon Finder and stack XP buffs until you reach level 50.
sections.need: You'll need: any character; a Crown Experience Scroll or Psijic Ambrosia is optional.

steps.t: Complete quests for experience.
steps.q: Completing quests, discovering new locations

steps.t: Discover new locations for experience.
steps.q: discovering new locations and completing their Objectives

steps.t: Queue for a group dungeon through the **Dungeon Finder** while under level 50 to get the Looking for Group buff.
steps.q: Entering a group dungeon through the Dungeon Finder while under level 50 will give you the "Looking for Group" buff

steps.t: Pick up dungeon quests: they reward 2.25 times the standard quest XP.
steps.q: so reward 2.25× the standard XP for a quest at that level

steps.t: Run a random dungeon through the **Dungeon Finder** for extra rewards and experience when the final boss dies.
q: The Undaunted also offer rewards for completing random dungeons through the dungeon finder.
The rewards and experience are automatically sent to you the moment the final boss of the dungeon dies.

steps.t: Use a Crown Experience Scroll or Psijic Ambrosia for a 50, 100 or 150% bonus; only one of the two works at a time.
steps.q: 50/100/150% Crown Experience Scroll — the same buff as Psijic Ambrosia, so only one or the other can be used

steps.t: Group with other players for 10% more XP from kills.
steps.q: 10% Grouping — applies only to XP from kills

steps.t: Activate [[The Apprentice]] Mundus Stone for an 8% bonus to experience.
q: The Apprentice now grants an 8% bonus to experience and inspiration gain, rather than Spell Damage.
Activating one will grant you a permanent blessing, although only one blessing can be active at a time.

steps.t: Open the **Character Sheet** to choose a harder Challenge Difficulty for overland, story instances, delves and public dungeons.
steps.q: From the Character Sheet, you can choose between three additional difficulties which will be applied in overland encounters, story instances, delves, and public dungeons

steps.t: If you pick Seasoned, plan for 100% more damage taken and 20% more experience from monsters.
steps.q: You will take 100% more damage from monsters and do 50% less damage. You will receive 50% more gold and 20% more experience from monsters.

steps.t: Reach level 50 to unlock Veteran content and get 10 Champion Points.
steps.q: Players can attain a maximum level of 50. Upon reaching the maximum level, players unlock Veteran content and receive 10 points into the Champion system.

sections.check: Your character shows level 50 and the Champion system opens with 10 points.

more.t: The Looking for Group buff gives 25% more Max Health and 20% more Weapon and Spell Damage.
more.q: increases your Max Health by 25% and your Weapon and Spell Damage by 20%

more.t: A kill gives you experience only if you dealt at least 3% of the enemy's maximum health in damage.
more.q: Killing enemies and helping others kill enemies (including by healing them) give experience so long as you deal at least 3% of the enemy's maximum health in damage

more.t: Picking locks and completing Encounters also give experience.
more.q: picking locks, and completing Encounters also grant experience

more.t: Equip gear with the Training trait for 2.5 to 86% more XP from kills.
more.q: 2.5–86% Training Trait — applies only to XP from kills

more.t: Wear Rings of Mara in a group for 10% more XP.
more.q: 10% Rings of Mara — requires grouping when worn

more.t: Overland [[Cyrodiil]], outside delves and Imperial City, gives a flat 25% XP boost.
more.q: In addition to these the overland part of Cyrodiil, excluding Delves and Imperial City, has a flat-rate boost of 25%.

more.t: Stacked XP buffs can reach a total increase of 290% for most content.
more.q: It is currently possible to stack XP buffs for a total possible increase of 290% for most types of content.

more.t: Master difficulty gives 75% more experience; Vestige gives 100% more.
q: You will receive 100% more gold and 75% more experience from monsters.
You will receive 200% more gold and 100% more experience from monsters.

more.t: Every level gives an attribute point; levels that are multiples of 5 give two and multiples of 10 give three.
q: Each level that a player gains allows them to allocate an attribute point to their magicka, health or stamina.
Levels that are a multiple of 5 grant two Attribute Points
Levels that are a multiple of 10 grant three Attribute Points

sections.title: How to collect skill points
sections.answer: Level up, absorb Skyshards and finish storyline quests.
sections.need: You'll need: time to explore and quest; no items are required.

steps.t: Level your character to 50 to earn 64 skill points.
steps.q: Leveling your character, up to level 50 (64 Skill Points)

steps.t: Absorb Skyshards: every three you collect give one skill point.
steps.q: However, you will receive one skill point for every three Skyshards you collect.

steps.t: Open the **Achievements** menu to read the clue for each Skyshard's location.
steps.q: In-game, clues to each Skyshard's location are listed in the Achievements menu under their respective areas.

steps.t: Finish the main quest for 11 skill points.
steps.q: Completing quests in the main quest (11 Skill Points)

steps.t: Complete the alliance zone storylines: 15 in Dominion, 16 in Covenant, 15 in Pact and 3 in [[Coldharbour]].
steps.q: Completing quest chains in the Dominion, Covenant, Pact, and Coldharbour main storylines (3 in Coldharbour: 16 in Covenant, 15 in Pact, 15 in Dominion)

steps.t: Complete the story quest in each group dungeon; the base game has 24 of these points.
steps.q: Completing the story quest in group dungeons (24 Skill Points in the base game, one for each completed dungeon storyline quest

steps.t: Complete the group challenges in public dungeons for 18 base game skill points.
steps.q: Completing group challenges in public dungeons (18 Skill Points in the base game

steps.t: Rank up in the Alliance War for up to 50 skill points.
steps.q: Ranking up in the Alliance War (50 Skill Points)

steps.t: Accept the Folium Discognitum in the [[Mages Guild]] quest chain to get 2 skill points.
q: Reading the Folium Discognitum (Optional quest reward from Mages Guild quest chain) (2 Skill Points)
Two of the skill points listed above are unobtainable if you decide not to accept the Folium Discognitum in the Mages Guild questline.

steps.t: Finish the [[Thieves Guild]] primary quest chain for 6 skill points.
steps.q: Completing the primary quest chain of the Thieves Guild storyline (6 Skill Points)

steps.t: Finish the [[Dark Brotherhood]] primary quest chain for 8 skill points.
steps.q: Completing the primary quest chain of the Dark Brotherhood storyline (8 Skill Points)

steps.t: Reallocate spent points from the **Skills** screen at no cost.
steps.q: As of Update 49, spent skill points can be reallocated directly from the Skills screen at no cost.

sections.check: Each Skyshard trio, level-up or storyline finish adds points you can spend on the Skills screen.

more.t: The current total is 579 skill points, counting all Chapters and DLCs.
more.q: up to a current total of 579 points including all Chapters and other DLCs

more.t: Skyshards give 113 skill points in the base game.
more.q: Absorbing skyshards (113 Skill Points in the base game

more.t: Collecting every Skyshard in one location also grants an Achievement.
more.q: Collecting all the Skyshards in one location grants you an Achievement.

more.t: The Necrom storyline gives 9 skill points and the West Weald storyline gives 5.
q: Completing the Necrom storyline (9 Skill Points)
Completing the West Weald storyline (5 Skill Points)

more.t: The Eastern Solstice storyline gives 6 skill points.
more.q: Completing the Eastern Solstice storyline (6 Skill Points)

more.t: Completing all Scribing quests gives 1 skill point.
more.q: Completing all Scribing quests (1 Skill point)

more.t: After you reach the maximum level, you no longer get skill points from leveling.
more.q: Characters will no longer receive attribute points and skill points to allocate

sections.title: How to choose which skill lines to level first
sections.answer: Know how each skill line levels and what it needs to unlock, then slot or wear what you want to raise.
sections.need: You'll need: level 10 for the Undaunted; the Summerset story quest for the Psijic Order.

steps.t: Slot at least one active skill from a class skill line on your current bar to level that line.
steps.q: To advance in the skill line, at least one active skill from the skill line must be slotted

steps.t: Hold a weapon to level its weapon skill line whenever you gain experience.
steps.q: Any class can advance in any of the Weapon skill lines by holding the appropriate weapon at the moment of gaining experience

steps.t: Slot more skills from that weapon line to level it faster.
steps.q: with more slotted skills granting faster advancement

steps.t: Wear at least 1 piece of [[Light Armor]], [[Medium Armor]] or [[Heavy Armor]] to level that line; more pieces level it faster.
steps.q: Only 1 piece need be worn, but progress will be faster the more pieces you wear of that type.

steps.t: Join the [[Fighters Guild]] by speaking to a recruiter in any Fighters Guild hall.
steps.q: To join, go to any Fighters Guild hall and speak with Aicessar, Basile Fenandre, or Hilan (regardless of your alliance) and tell them you're ready to join.

steps.t: Kill undead, Daedra or werewolves to level the [[Fighters Guild]] line.
steps.q: Fighters Guild progress is gained by killing undeads, Daedra or werewolves anywhere, and by doing daily quests to clear Dark Anchors.

steps.t: Join the [[Mages Guild]] by speaking to a recruiter in any Mages Guild hall.
steps.q: To join, go to any Mages Guild hall and speak with Curinure, Nemarc, or Rudrasa (regardless of your alliance) and tell them you're ready to join.

steps.t: Read Lorebooks to level the [[Mages Guild]] line.
steps.q: Each Lorebook recovered grants 5, while completing a collection of lorebooks grants 20.

steps.t: Accept the Undaunted joining quest at level 10 or higher to unlock the [[Undaunted]] line.
q: A player must be at least level 10 to join the Undaunted
Accepting the quest will unlock the skill line.

steps.t: Complete dungeon quests, Pledges and delve dailies to level the [[Undaunted]] line.
steps.q: To level the skill-line, players gain reputation by completing Dungeon Achievements (not including those in the Public Dungeons section), Pledges and delve dailies.

steps.t: Complete The Queen's Decree in Shimmerene before you try to join the [[Psijic Order]].
steps.q: To join the Psijic Order, you must first complete the first Summerset zone story quest in Shimmerene, The Queen's Decree.

steps.t: Follow the Psijic Order storyline to level it; it has no repeatable quests.
steps.q: Psijic Order has no daily or otherwise repeatable quests, and progress is obtained only through the quest storyline.

steps.t: Earn Alliance War points to level [[Assault]] and [[Support]] together.
steps.q: Progress in the Assault and Support lines comes as you gain Alliance War points for any PVP or alliance-war related activities

sections.check: The skill line appears in your Skills menu and its rank rises as you play.

more.t: Your racial skill line levels with your character level.
more.q: Progress in the Racial skill lines is directly equivalent to your character's overall experience level.

more.t: Do the quest The Antiquarian Circle to unlock [[Excavation]] and [[Scrying]].
q: Excavation - obtained by the quest The Antiquarian Circle
Scrying - obtained by the quest The Antiquarian Circle

more.t: Progress through the main quest to unlock [[Soul Magic]].
more.q: Soul Magic - obtained by progress through the main quest

more.t: At character level 15 you unlock Weapon Swapping and 5 more skill slots.
more.q: At character level 15, when you acquire Weapon Swapping, you gain an additional 5 slots for your alternate weapon.

more.t: Each race gets a free passive that raises experience gain for one skill.
more.q: each race gets one free passive which increases their experience gain with a given skill.

more.t: The [[Fighters Guild]] Slayer passive raises Weapon and Spell Damage by 1% per slotted Fighters Guild ability at its first rank.
more.q: Increases your Weapon and Spell Damage by 1% for each Fighters Guild ability slotted.

more.t: The Undaunted Mettle passive ([[Undaunted]] line) raises Max Health, Stamina and Magicka by 1% per armor type you wear at its first rank.
more.q: Increases your Max Health, Stamina, and Magicka by 1% per type of Armor (Heavy, Medium, Light) that you have equipped.

more.t: The [[Psijic Order]] See the Unseen passive lets you interact with rifts across Tamriel.
more.q: You can now interact with rifts all throughout Tamriel.

more.t: The [[Discipline Artisan]] Champion star raises experience for active skills and their skill lines by 3% per stage.
more.q: Increases experience gain for currently active skills and their skill lines by 3% per stage.

sections.answer_data: There is no data-backed first pick: that needs a non-class line slotted by a quarter of the recent builds on each of two build sites, and only one site has recent build posts. The steps show how each line levels. Only ArzyelBuilds has build posts in the window (20, updated 2026-10-18 to 2026-11-18); they slot Fighters Guild in 90% and Two Handed in 70%. One site, no second recent source: read it as a count, not a recommendation.

sections.title: How to unlock and set up subclassing
sections.answer: Get one character to level 50, do the free quest A Study in Discipline, then swap up to two class skill lines.
sections.need: You'll need: at least one level 50 character on your account.

steps.t: Get at least one character to level 50.
steps.q: In order to use subclassing, you must first have at least one level 50 character

steps.t: Start the quest A Study in Discipline from the Crown Store at no cost.
steps.q: you can start the quest A Study in Discipline from the Crown Store (at no cost)

steps.t: Travel to the city for your alliance: Dune ([[Reaper's March]]), Evermore ([[Bangkorai]]) or Riften ([[The Rift]]).
steps.q: Dune (Reaper's March), Evermore (Bangkorai), Riften (The Rift)

steps.t: Talk to Bahtra at-Hunding at her campsite.
steps.q: travel to the following city depending on your alliance and talk to Bahtra at-Hunding at her campsite

steps.t: Ask her to unlock the subclassing menu.
steps.q: she will help you unlock the Subclassing system. This will take you to the subclassing menu

steps.t: Replace up to two of your class skill lines with lines from other classes.
steps.q: It allows a player to customize their character by replacing up to two of their class' skill lines with those from other classes.

steps.t: Budget two skill points for each stage of a subclassed line.
steps.q: A subclassed skill line gains access to all skills and passives in the same way as base class skill lines, although each stage costs two skill points instead of one.

steps.t: Level the subclassed lines once: their progress is shared by all characters on your account.
steps.q: progress in sub-classed skill lines is shared across all characters on your account.

steps.t: Keep no more than three unlevelled subclass skill lines at a time.
steps.q: You can have up to three unlevelled sub-class skill lines at a time

steps.t: Complete A Study in Discipline on each other character you want to subclass.
steps.q: the quest A Study in Discipline must be completed on each character whose base class skill lines you wish to change.

steps.t: If you want [[Class Mastery]] instead, keep all three native class lines; swapping any out refunds your Class Mastery purchases.
steps.q: Activating subclassing in any capacity by swapping out one or more of your native class skills will automatically refund and unlearn any currently active purchases from Class Mastery.

sections.check: Your Skills menu lists the new class skill line in place of the one you swapped out.

more.t: To use Class Mastery, reach level 50 in all three of your class skill lines and do not subclass.
q: Reach Level 50 in all three of the character's class skill lines.
for characters that have mastered (i.e. reached level 50) in all 3 of their native class skill lines and are not actively subclassing.

more.t: Each class has five Class Mastery passives, and each character can pick two.
more.q: Each class will have five different passive skills and for each character you will be able to pick two of them.

more.t: Class Mastery uses its own points, separate from skill points; you get 2 right away.
q: distinct from Skill Points, these are exclusively utilized in your Class Mastery skill line
For the time being you are limited to 2, which are both immediately granted.

more.t: Respec Class Mastery the same way as skill points, through Respec or the Armory.
more.q: the respec process is the same as normal skill points through the Respec or Armory systems.

more.t: The Class Mastery line stays hidden while you subclass and returns when you respec into all your native lines.
more.q: The skill line will also remain hidden while subclassing, only appearing again when you respec into all your native class skill lines.

more.t: If you do not want to subclass now, use the skip option in the quest giver's dialogue.
more.q: A new skip option is added to this quest in the bestower’s dialogue tree if you do not wish to subclass right now

more.t: A fully levelled subclass line counts as mastered, like a base class line.
more.q: once a subclass skill has been fully levelled, it is considered 'mastered' in the same way that base class skills can be mastered.

sections.title: How to earn and spend Champion Points
sections.answer: Earn experience at level 50, use your daily Enlightenment, then spend points in the Craft, Warfare and Fitness constellations and slot active perks.
sections.need: You'll need: one character at level 50.

steps.t: Reach level 50 on any character to unlock the Champion System.
steps.q: The Champion System is unlocked when one of your characters reaches Veteran rank at Level 50.

steps.t: Keep earning experience: from then on it gives Champion Points.
steps.q: From that point on, experience points provide progression in Champion Points.

steps.t: Play daily to use Enlightenment: you get 400,000 XP of it once per day.
steps.q: Once per day, you receive 400,000 XP of Enlightenment

steps.t: Earn up to 160 Champion Points to wear stronger gear and use stronger consumables.
steps.q: Gaining Champion Points allows players to equip more powerful gear and use more powerful consumables, up to the Champion Progression Cap of 160.

steps.t: Spend points across the three constellations: Craft, Warfare and Fitness.
steps.q: organized across three Guardian Constellations: Craft (Thief), Warfare (Mage), and Fitness (Warrior).

steps.t: Spend up to 1200 points in each constellation, for a cap of 3600.
steps.q: The current cap is 3600, and you are unable to spend any points that you have earned above this cap. This means you are able to spend 1200 points in each of the three constellations.

steps.t: Put points into the base active perks, up to 50 stages at 1 point per stage.
steps.q: These perks can be invested in up to 50 stages at 1 point per stage.

steps.t: Unlock base perks first, since most advanced perks require them.
steps.q: Most advanced perks require prerequisite investments in base constellation perks

steps.t: Slot your active perks on the **Champion Bar** at the top of each constellation.
q: Advanced abilities that must be equipped to the Champion Bar to function.
The Champion Bar appears at the top of each constellation interface

steps.t: Swap slotted perks while out of combat; you do not need to respec.
steps.q: Perks can be swapped anytime while out of combat, allowing build flexibility without respeccing Champion Points.

steps.t: If you ride a lot, slot [[War Mount]] to remove mount Stamina costs outside combat.
steps.q: Improves your mastery with mounts, removing all mount Stamina costs outside of combat.

sections.check: Your Champion Bar shows the perks you slotted, and the Champion menu shows your spent points.

more.t: While you are Enlightened, you gain four times the experience.
more.q: While you are Enlightened, experience gain is multiplied by four

more.t: Since Update 45, many Craft perks are passive and do not need a slot.
more.q: As of Update 45, many formerly slottable Craft tree perks became passive, eliminating the need for constant swapping during different activities.

more.t: Your Enlightenment pool caps at 4,800,000 XP after twelve days.
more.q: Enlightenment accumulates in a pool with a cap of 4,800,000 XP after twelve days.

more.t: The Enlightenment pool is shared by all your level 50 characters.
more.q: the Enlightenment pool is shared across all Level 50 characters on your account.

more.t: Your account keeps Champion Points even if you delete all your level 50 characters.
more.q: Once you have access to Champion Points on an account, you will always have access to them, even if you delete all of your Level 50 characters.

more.t: Save your Champion Points in an Armory build to swap them quickly.
more.q: This allows you to quickly change your attributes, skills, equipment, Champion Points, and Outfits.

more.t: [[Wrathful Strikes]] in Warfare grants 41 Weapon and Spell Damage to damaging abilities per stage.
more.q: Grants 41 Weapon and Spell Damage to your damaging abilities per stage.

more.t: [[Boundless Vitality]] in Fitness grants 28 Max Health per stage.
more.q: Grants 28 Max Health per stage.

more.t: [[Gifted Rider]] in Craft increases Mount Speed by 2% per stage.
more.q: Increases your Mount Speed by 2% per stage.

sections.title: How to train your mount every day
sections.answer: Talk to a stablemaster once a day and raise one riding stat.
sections.need: You'll need: at least one mount.

steps.t: Get a mount before you try to train.
steps.q: A single mount is needed before you can increase your Riding Skill.

steps.t: Go to a stable in a city.
steps.q: These are places where you can find stablemasters and make use of their services.

steps.t: Speak with the stablemaster to train your Riding Skill.
steps.q: You can train your character's Riding Skill once per day by speaking with stablemasters

steps.t: Pay 250 gold for each training.
steps.q: Each upgrade costs 250 Gold.

steps.t: If you want to move faster while mounted, pick Speed.
steps.q: Speed: Determines the speed at which you move while mounted.

steps.t: If you want to take more hits before you are knocked off, pick Stamina.
steps.q: You will be forced to dismount if hit when this stat is at zero, so upgrading stamina will allow you to take more damage before this happens.

steps.t: If you want more bag space, pick Capacity for 1 more slot each time.
steps.q: Each upgrade increases your inventory capacity by 1 point.

steps.t: Keep training until each stat reaches its cap of 60.
steps.q: There are three stats available for increase, and each can be raised to a maximum of 60

steps.t: Come back after the daily reset: 3am UTC on EU, 10am UTC on NA.
steps.q: The reset occurs at 3am UTC on EU servers, and 10am UTC on NA servers.

steps.t: Train every character on its own, because the bonus belongs to the character, not the mount.
steps.q: are bound to the character rather than the mount, making the different mount types cosmetic.

sections.check: The stat you picked shows one point higher out of its cap of 60.

more.t: Buy Riding Lessons from the Crown Store if you want to train faster than once a day.
more.q: Riding Lessons can also be purchased from the Crown Store in order to speed up the training process.

more.t: Reach 20 points in a stat to get a cosmetic upgrade on your mounts.
more.q: After 20 points in a single stat, a cosmetic upgrade will be applied to your mounts

more.t: Slot the [[War Mount]] Champion star to remove mount Stamina costs outside of combat.
more.q: Improves your mastery with mounts, removing all mount Stamina costs outside of combat.

sections.title: How to research traits
sections.answer: Research a trait by giving up an item that has it at the matching crafting station.
sections.need: You'll need: an item with the trait you want, in your bag or bank.

steps.t: Get an item that has the trait you want.
steps.q: To start the research process, you need to have an item with the desired trait in your inventory or bank.

steps.t: Use an item you found or one another player crafted.
steps.q: Both found items and items crafted by other players work.

steps.t: Go to the station that matches the item: Clothing, Woodworking, Blacksmithing or Jewelry Crafting.
q: Light and medium armor at Clothing stations
Bows, staves and shields at Woodworking stations
Heavy armor and metal weapons at Blacksmithing stations
Necklaces and rings at Jewelry Crafting stations

steps.t: Start the research, knowing that the item is destroyed.
steps.q: Researching a trait will destroy the item.

steps.t: Research each item type on its own, since a trait unlocks only for that type.
steps.q: Researching a trait will unlock it only for that particular type of item

steps.t: Research on each character, since research does not carry over to your other characters.
steps.q: researching a trait on one character does not unlock that trait on any other character on that account.

steps.t: Plan for 2 hours on the first trait of an item type, with each further trait doubling the time.
steps.q: The base research time for a trait is 2 hours real time. Each further trait you research for an item type doubles this time

steps.t: Log off if you like, because research keeps counting down.
steps.q: Research time continues to count down while you are not playing the character that is researching (e.g. playing another character or offline).

steps.t: Put skill points into Metallurgy, Stitching, Carpentry or Lapidary Research to research up to 25% faster.
steps.q: These abilities can increase the research speed by up to 25%, and raise the limit of concurrent research tasks to 3

steps.t: Use those passives to research up to 3 traits at once per craft, except in Jewelry Crafting.
steps.q: raise the limit of concurrent research tasks to 3 (with the exception of Lapidary Research, which does not add additional research slots)

steps.t: Research only one trait per item type at a time.
steps.q: you still cannot research multiple traits on a single item type at the same time.

sections.check: The item is gone and a research timer for that trait starts counting down.

more.t: At its top rank, Metallurgy reduces research times by 25%, limits research time to 10 days, and allows three items at once.
more.q: Reduces research times by 25%, limits research time to 10 days, and allows the research of three items at once.

more.t: Use a research scroll to cut the timers of everything you are researching in that craft.
more.q: Using a research scroll will reduce the timers of all items currently being researched in one or more crafts by an amount dependent on the scroll

more.t: Expect a 20 hour cooldown on scrolls from Rolis Hlaalu, and none on Crown Store scrolls.
more.q: Scrolls obtained from the Crown Store have no cooldown between uses; scrolls purchased from Rolis Hlaalu have a cooldown of 20 hours.

sections.title: How to craft a set
sections.answer: Craft set gear at that set's special crafting site, once you know enough traits for the item.
sections.need: You'll need: enough researched traits, crafting materials and a known style motif.

steps.t: Find the crafting site of the set you want.
steps.q: To craft set items, you must find one of their special crafting sites.

steps.t: Look for a site in your own alliance's territory.
steps.q: For most sets, there is one crafting site in each Alliance's territory.

steps.t: If the site is in a DLC zone, get that DLC first.
steps.q: Some crafting sites are found in DLC zones, and can only be accessed if you own the DLC.

steps.t: Research enough traits for the item type you want to make.
steps.q: to craft a set item, you must have researched a number of traits for that specific item type.

steps.t: Use the site's blacksmithing, clothing, jewelry or woodworking station that fits the item.
steps.q: special Crafting Sites that are equipped with blacksmithing, clothing, jewelry, and woodworking stations for crafting items in specific Sets.

steps.t: Learn the Crafting Motif for the style you want.
q: A style can be used if the corresponding crafting motif is known for that item.
Crafting Motifs are books that unlock the ability to craft an item in a certain style through blacksmithing, clothing, or woodworking.

steps.t: Refine raw materials 10 at a time to get crafting materials.
steps.q: raw materials for four different crafting professions (blacksmithing, clothing, jewelry crafting, and woodworking) may be refined, 10 at a time, into 7-10 refined craftable items

steps.t: Keep the upgrade items that refining also gives you.
steps.q: refining raw materials will also yield trait items and upgrading items, which can improve the quality crafted items

steps.t: Improve the finished piece with tempers to raise its quality.
steps.q: the piece can be augmented even more through the use of tempers. These elements can enhance the value and quality of your work.

steps.t: Put points into Temper Expertise to raise your chance to improve items.
steps.q: Increases the chances of improving items with tempers.

sections.check: The new piece shows the set name and the trait you chose.

more.t: A failed improve attempt can break the item.
more.q: Trying to improve an item can result in breaks, so be careful!

more.t: Expect all crafted gear to bind when you equip it.
more.q: if someone else crafts the gear for you. All crafted gear is bind-on-equip.

more.t: Attune an Attunable Crafting Station at a set's site to craft that set at home.
more.q: go to one of the sites described in 1, and attune your stations to that Set. Then you can have stations in your home that can craft that Set.
