more.t: Find all fourteen chapters of a partial motif to unlock the whole style.
more.q: Partial motifs are divided into fourteen chapters, each of which must be found and read to unlock all parts of that style.

more.t: Use your own race's style, which you already know.
more.q: Every player begins the game having already "learned" the racial motif associated with their race.

sections.title: How to do daily crafting writs
sections.answer: Get certified, take one writ per craft each day from a writ board, craft it and turn it in.
sections.need: You'll need: a character of at least level 6.

steps.t: Reach at least level 6.
steps.q: All certifications require the character to be at least level 6.

steps.t: Read the new notice on a board in a major city to start certification.
steps.q: When you reach level six a new notice will appear on the noticeboards in all major cities.

steps.t: Do the short certification quest for each craft you want.
steps.q: The certification process involves a short quest where you are required to craft an item for a master crafter NPC, and serves as a tutorial to the crafting systems.

steps.t: If you already have Rank 10 in a craft, skip the tutorial part.
steps.q: If you are already an established crafter, and have reached Rank 10 in a particular crafting skill line, you can skip the tutorial section and become certified immediately.

steps.t: If you want Jewelry Crafting writs, get certified in Alinor in [[Summerset]].
steps.q: this certification requires access to Alinor in Summerset

steps.t: Go to a writ board in a major town or city.
steps.q: Crafting Writs can be accepted from writs boards located in major towns and cities.

steps.t: Use the **Consumables Crafting Writs** board for alchemy, enchanting and provisioning writs.
q: When activating the Consumables Crafting Writs board, you'll be greeted with:
Potions, Glyphs, Food, and Drink! Hone your craft and earn a reward!

steps.t: Use the **Equipment Crafting Writs** board for blacksmithing, clothing, woodworking and jewelry writs.
q: When activating the Equipment Crafting Writs board, you'll be greeted with:
Blacksmith Writ: Fulfill a contract to deliver blacksmithing goods.

steps.t: Craft the requested gear at a regular crafting station.
steps.q: Arms and armor are always requested at the lowest quality, with no additional trait and can be created at regular Crafting Stations.

steps.t: Deliver the finished items: each writ is a contract to deliver them.
steps.q: Alchemist Writ: Fulfill a contract to deliver alchemical products.

steps.t: Collect your reward: experience, gold, a box of supplies and inspiration.
steps.q: Successful completion of a crafting writ will reward experience, gold, a consumable box of supplies, and inspiration for that profession.

steps.t: Come back after the reset at 3am UTC on EU or 10am UTC on NA, since you get one writ per craft per day.
q: One writ for each profession may be completed per day.
daily writs reset at 3am UTC on EU servers, and 10am UTC on NA servers.

sections.check: The writ quest leaves your journal and the reward box is in your bag.

more.t: Look for Survey Reports in writ rewards, except from Provisioner writs.
more.q: The rewards for fulfilling crafting writs, except Provisioner writs, may randomly include Survey Reports, which are similar to Treasure Maps.

more.t: Expect a survey about 1 in 8 times.
more.q: Surveys have an approximate 1 in 8 chance of dropping, regardless of level of crafting writ completed.

more.t: Watch for Master Writs after you finish a top-tier writ.
more.q: Master writs are special writs that can be rewarded to you after completing a normal top-tier writ.

more.t: Spend Writ Vouchers from Master Writs at Rolis Hlaalu.
more.q: Completing a Master Writ will reward you with Writ Vouchers, which can be used to buy special or unique items from Rolis Hlaalu, the Mastercraft Mediator.

more.t: Turn in Master Writs in an alliance capital.
more.q: Master Writs can only be dropped off in the capital city of an alliance.

more.t: Learn all 9 traits of a craft to raise your Master Writ drop chance.
more.q: Learning all 9 crafting traits for the appropriate craft.

sections.title: How to get the gear you want
sections.answer: Farm each set type where it drops, then use Transmute Crystals to change traits or reconstruct pieces you have collected.
sections.need: You'll need: Transmute Crystals and a Transmute Station.

steps.t: Farm overland sets in the zone they drop from.
q: Each set has a specific zone that it drops from.
Set items can be found from World Bosses, delve monsters, public dungeon monsters, dolmens (or other world events) and treasure chests found within the zone.

steps.t: Run Group Dungeons for dungeon sets.
steps.q: Dungeon Sets can be found from normal and veteran Group Dungeons. Bosses and minibosses will always drop pieces from these sets in specific slots.

steps.t: Run Trials for trial sets.
steps.q: Trial Sets are available from any of the Trials in the game. Bosses in Trials will drop pieces of these sets.

steps.t: Get a monster helm from the last boss of its dungeon on Veteran.
steps.q: The head pieces are guaranteed drops from the associated last boss of a group dungeon on Veteran difficulty

steps.t: Do Undaunted pledges to earn keys.
steps.q: Completing a normal or veteran mode Pledge for a base game dungeon will reward you with a key.

steps.t: Buy monster shoulders from the Pledge Masters with Undaunted Keys.
steps.q: shoulder pieces can be bought from Pledge Masters for Undaunted Keys

steps.t: Find all five fragments of a Mythic item through Antiquities.
steps.q: All mythic items are broken up into five fragments which each need to be found to create the final piece.

steps.t: Earn Transmute Crystals from Trials, Group Dungeons, Battlegrounds, Tales of Tribute or the Alliance War.
steps.q: Transmute Crystals, which can be acquired from a variety of activities, including Trials, Group Dungeons, Battlegrounds, Tales of Tribute, and participating in the Alliance War in Cyrodiil.

steps.t: Go to a Transmute Station in [[Clockwork City]], a Mages Guild hall or [[Eyevea]].
q: with Update 50 Transmute Stations were added to all the Mages Guild Halls as well as Eyevea.
Transmute Stations can be found in Clockwork City and in various Mages guild halls

steps.t: Research the trait you want first.
steps.q: To reconstruct an item with a trait, or transform an item's trait, the desired trait must have been researched in the appropriate Crafting skill line.

steps.t: Spend 50 Transmute Crystals to change an item's trait.
steps.q: 50 Transmute Crystals are used to change the traits of armor and weapons to a trait previously researched for that item.

steps.t: Reconstruct a set piece from your collection for 25 to 75 crystals, less as you collect more of the set.
steps.q: It is 25 crystals if all items in the set are known, 75 if only one item is known (unless it's a 1 item set)

sections.check: The item shows the trait you picked, and your crystal count goes down.

more.t: Run group or solo Arenas for arena sets.
more.q: Arena Sets are five-piece sets that can be found from group and solo Arenas.

more.t: Buy PvP sets with Alliance Points or Tel Var stones.
more.q: PVP Sets can be purchased using Alliance Points or Tel Var stones.

more.t: Wear only one Mythic item at a time.
more.q: Only one mythic item can be worn at a time

more.t: Join the Antiquarian Circle in Solitude to start Antiquities.
more.q: To begin treasure hunting, you first need to join the Antiquarian Circle. To do this, travel to Solitude and speak to Verita Numida

more.t: Reach level 7 in [[Scrying]] with Antiquarian Insight IV to scry Mythic leads.
more.q: You are required to be at least level 7 in Scrying, and have the Antiquarian Insight IV passive to scry Master difficulty leads.

more.t: Spend crystals before you hit the cap of 1,500, or 3,000 with ESO Plus.
more.q: Only 1,500 Transmute Crystals can be held at once per account (3,000 with ESO Plus), and they are bound to the account.

more.t: Expect transmuted and reconstructed items to be bound.
more.q: Transmuted and reconstructed items are bound, and cannot be sold or traded to other players.

sections.title: How to pick and use a Mundus Stone
sections.answer: Activate a Mundus Stone to get its blessing; only one blessing is active at a time.
sections.need: You'll need: to travel to a zone that has the stone you want.

steps.t: Find a Mundus Stone, a standing stone tied to a Constellation.
steps.q: Mundus Stones are standing stones dedicated to the Constellations.

steps.t: Activate it to get its permanent blessing.
steps.q: Activating one will grant you a permanent blessing, although only one blessing can be active at a time.

steps.t: Activate a different stone to change your blessing.
steps.q: Interact with a Mundus Stone and change your Mundus boon.

steps.t: Look in [[Cyrodiil]] for any stone except [[The Lord]].
steps.q: The Lord is the only stone not found in Cyrodiil.

steps.t: Skip DLC zones, because they have no Mundus Stones.
steps.q: No DLC zones contain any Mundus Stones whatsoever

steps.t: If you want Weapon and Spell Damage, use [[The Warrior]] in [[Malabal Tor]], [[Alik'r Desert]], [[Eastmarch]] or [[Cyrodiil]].
q: The Warrior now grants both Weapon and Spell Damage, rather than only Weapon Damage.
that stone can be found in Malabal Tor, the Alik'r Desert, Eastmarch, or in Cyrodiil.

steps.t: If you want 8% more experience and inspiration gain, use [[The Apprentice]].
steps.q: The Apprentice now grants an 8% bonus to experience and inspiration gain, rather than Spell Damage.

steps.t: Wear armor with the Divines trait to boost your stone's effect.
steps.q: Armor with the Divines Trait increases the effect of Mundus Stones, depending on the Armor's quality.

steps.t: If you wear the [[Twice-Born Star]] set, take two blessings at once.
steps.q: The Twice-Born Star set allows a character to have two blessings at the same time.

sections.check: Your new blessing replaces the old one.

more.t: Ignore the three broken stones in [[Craglorn]], because they can't change your blessing.
more.q: There are three unmarked, broken Mundus Stones in Craglorn dedicated to the Lord, Lady and Steed. They are related to the quest The Corrupted Stone and can't be used to change blessings.

sections.title: How to use food and potions
sections.answer: Eat food or drink for a timed stat buff, and use potions for quick restores and buffs.
sections.need: You'll need: food, drink or potions that you bought, found or crafted.

steps.t: Eat food to raise your Health, Magicka or Stamina for a while.
steps.q: Food items boost at least one of the three stats, Health, Magicka, or Stamina for a period of time.

steps.t: Drink a beverage to regenerate stats faster for a while.
steps.q: Drinks provide more rapid regeneration of at least one of the three stats over a period of time.

steps.t: Keep one food buff, because different foods do not stack.
steps.q: If different entries are consumed one after another, the effects do not stack.

steps.t: If you buy food from Innkeepers or Chefs, expect it to be weaker than crafted food.
q: they may be purchased from Innkeepers or Chefs
They are less potent than their crafted versions.

steps.t: Learn a recipe before you try to cook it.
steps.q: in Provisioning you must have found and learned a recipe before you are able to create any Food or Drink.

steps.t: Cook at a Cooking Fire.
steps.q: You must be at a Cooking Fire in order to create any items.

steps.t: If you want all three stats, cook a Complex Recipe.
steps.q: Complex Recipes are more powerful, and will affect all three stats.

steps.t: Pick up potions from merchants, containers and slain enemies.
steps.q: Potions of various types can be found in many places, for sale by general Merchants, in containers, in Alchemy Bottles loose on tables, etc., and on the corpses of your slain enemies.

steps.t: Craft potions at an Alchemy station to get stronger ones than you find.
steps.q: In all cases, these will be weaker than the ones you can craft yourself at Alchemy stations

steps.t: Combine 1 solvent with 2-3 reagents at the alchemy table.
steps.q: Creating potions in ESO involves combining 1 solvent with 2-3 reagents at the alchemy table.

steps.t: Pick two reagents that share an effect.
steps.q: two reagents with the same effect need to be combined in order to craft a potion.

steps.t: Use a water-based solvent to make a potion you can drink.
steps.q: A water-based solvent creates a potion that you can drink to receive its effects

sections.check: The food or potion buff shows on your character with its timer.

more.t: Expect vendor food to last 35 minutes with a 5 second cooldown.
more.q: Items on this list increase an attribute maximum value for 35 minutes and have a 5 second cooldown.

more.t: Eat a reagent to learn its first effect.
more.q: You are also able to eat potion ingredients to discover their first effect.

more.t: Use an oil-based solvent to make poisons for your weapons.
more.q: an oil-based solvent creates poisons which can be applied to your weapons to cause negative effects on your enemies.

more.t: Note that Damage and Critical potions now give both the Weapon and Spell versions.
more.q: Damage and Critical are now hybridized, so potions that previously applied only Weapon or Spell versions now provide both.

sections.title: How to fight well (the combat basics)
sections.answer: Light attack to build Ultimate, heavy attack to get resources back, block heavy hits, roll out of red areas and break free from stuns.
sections.need: You'll need: any weapon and enough Stamina for blocking, dodging and breaking free.

steps.t: Tap the attack button to light attack.
steps.q: It is performed by tapping the attack button.

steps.t: Keep light attacking in combat: each hit gives a hidden buff that makes 3 Ultimate every second for 9 seconds.
steps.q: Hitting a light attack while in combat gives you a hidden buff which generates 3 Ultimate every second for 9 seconds

steps.t: Hold the attack button to heavy attack.
steps.q: Heavy attacks are performed by holding the attack button.

steps.t: Fully charge a heavy attack to restore Magicka (with a staff) or Stamina (other weapons).
steps.q: Heavy attacks restore Magicka (with staves) or Stamina (other weapons) when fully charged.

steps.t: Hold block to take less damage and stop the disabling effects of most attacks.
steps.q: For most attacks, a successful block will reduce your damage taken and prevent any negative disabling effects associated with that attack.

steps.t: Block an enemy's heavy attack to set it Off Balance.
steps.q: Blocking an enemy's heavy attack will set it Off Balance.

steps.t: Heavy attack an Off Balance enemy to knock it down for 70% more damage.
steps.q: Using a heavy attack against an Off Balance opponent will knock them down, deal 70% more damage and restore double the resources.

steps.t: Interrupt an enemy who winds up an attack while you are in melee range.
steps.q: Players can interrupt an opponent who is winding up an attack, as long as they are within melee range.

steps.t: Roll dodge out of red areas on the ground.
q: Area of Effect attacks are often indicated as red areas.
Roll dodging allows the player to roll in a given direction in order to escape an area of effect or break free of a rooting effect.

steps.t: Space out your rolls: each roll adds dodge roll fatigue, which makes the next roll cost more.
steps.q: Performing a roll dodge will give the player dodge roll fatigue, increasing the cost of consecutive rolls until the effect dissipates.

steps.t: Break free when you are stunned to get crowd control immunity for 7 seconds.
q: Players can break free of some forms of crowd controlling effects, such as stuns.
which makes them immune to crowd control effects for 7 seconds

steps.t: Swap between your two combat bars once you reach level 15.
steps.q: Once a player reaches level 15, they can switch between two combat bars.

sections.check: Your Ultimate bar fills while you fight, and enemies whose heavy attacks you block show white swirls (Off Balance).

more.t: Press the attack key while blocking to bash; a bash interrupts enemies.
q: Pressing the attack key while blocking does a Bash.
It interrupts enemies and can trigger your weapon's poisons and enchantments.

more.t: Activate an ally's synergy when the prompt shows at the bottom of the screen.
more.q: a prompt at the bottom of the screen appears letting you know that you can activate a Synergy

more.t: Wait 20 seconds before you use the same synergy again.
more.q: Synergies have a 20 second cooldown per player for each individual Synergy.

more.t: Gain Ultimate by hitting enemies, healing others, blocking or dodging.
more.q: Ultimate regeneration triggers upon hitting a non-trivial enemy with Light or Heavy attacks, when healing others (healing yourself does not count), or upon blocking or dodging an attack.

more.t: Spend your Ultimate before 500: that is the most you can store.
more.q: The maximum Ultimate that you can accumulate is 500.

more.t: Move out of damage-over-time areas: you cannot block them.
more.q: Damage from areas dealing damage over time (DoT) like Wall of Elements and effects that are on or inside characters such as Daedric Curse cannot be blocked.

more.t: Reassign your attribute points from the Character screen for free (since Update 49).
more.q: Beginning with Update 49, attribute points can be reassigned from the Character screen at no cost.

more.t: Do not raise max Stamina to make blocking or dodging cheaper: it does not change their cost.
more.q: Having more maximum stamina will not increase the cost of dodging, blocking, or other combat maneuvers

sections.title: How to read buffs, debuffs and penetration
sections.answer: Buffs help you and allies, debuffs hurt enemies; a Major and a Minor of the same type stack, two of the same name do not, and Update 51 merged Sorcery into Brutality and Prophecy into Savagery.
sections.need: You'll need: your buff bar and the enemy's debuff bar in view.

steps.t: Read buffs as effects on you or your allies, and debuffs as effects on enemies.
steps.q: Buffs are applied to yourself or your allies, and debuffs are applied to enemies.

steps.t: Avoid two sources of the same buff: buffs with the same name from different sources do not stack.
steps.q: Two buffs/debuffs with the same name from different sources will not stack

steps.t: Combine a Major and a Minor buff of the same type: those do stack.
steps.q: though a Major and Minor buff of the same type will

steps.t: Look for Brutality to raise both Weapon and Spell Damage: Sorcery has been removed and replaced with Brutality.
steps.q: Brutality now provides both weapon and spell damage, while Sorcery has been removed and replaced with Brutality.

steps.t: Look for Savagery to raise both Weapon and Spell Critical chance: Prophecy was removed and replaced with Savagery.
steps.q: Savagery now provides both weapon and spell critical chance, while Prophecy has been removed and replaced with Savagery.

steps.t: Bring a Dragonknight for Minor Brutality from the Elder Dragon passive: 10% more Weapon and Spell Damage.
steps.q: The Dragonknight Elder Dragon passive continues to grant Minor Brutality, which now increases both Weapon and Spell Damage by 10%.

steps.t: Bring a Nightblade for Minor Savagery from the Hemorrhage passive: 6% more Weapon and Spell Critical Chance.
steps.q: The Nightblade Hemorrhage passive continues to grant Minor Savagery, which now increases both Weapon and Spell Critical Chance by 6%.

steps.t: Bring a Sorcerer for the Exploitation passive: 2974 Offensive Penetration.
steps.q: The Sorcerer Exploitation passive no longer grants Minor Prophecy, and instead provides a unique 2974 Offensive Penetration buff.

steps.t: Bring a Templar for the Illuminate passive: 2974 Armor.
steps.q: The Templar Illuminate passive no longer grants Minor Sorcery, and instead provides a unique 2974 Armor buff.

steps.t: Add penetration so more of your damage breaks through enemy armor.
steps.q: Penetration is a value that represents how much of your damage will break through an opponent's armor.

steps.t: Use Minor Force for 10% more critical damage, or Major Force for 20% (wiki values that may predate the Update 51 buff overhaul).
q: Increases critical damage done by 10%.
Increases critical damage done by 20%.
Buffs have been overhauled with Update 51, page needs to be updated

sections.check: With a Major and a Minor of one type active, you see both on your buff bar.

more.t: Critical damage starts at 50% and is capped at 125%.
more.q: Critical Damage starts with a base damage increase of 50%, and is capped at 125%.

more.t: An enemy with 18,200 armor resists 36.4% of your damage.
more.q: For example, if an enemy NPC has 18,200 armor, they will resist 36.4% of your damage.

more.t: Check exact buff values in game: the wiki's Buffs page says buffs were overhauled with Update 51 and the page needs updating.
more.q: Buffs have been overhauled with Update 51, page needs to be updated

more.t: Look for Minor Resolve to gain 2974 physical and spell resistance (value from the wiki Buffs page, which says it is not yet updated for Update 51).
q: Increases physical and spell resistance by 2974.
Buffs have been overhauled with Update 51, page needs to be updated

more.t: Look for Major Resolve to gain 5948 physical and spell resistance (value from the wiki Buffs page, which says it is not yet updated for Update 51).
q: Increases physical and spell resistance by 5948.
Buffs have been overhauled with Update 51, page needs to be updated

more.t: Put Minor Breach on enemies to cut their physical and spell resistance by 2974 (value from the wiki Buffs page, which says it is not yet updated for Update 51).
q: Decreases target's physical and spell resistance by 2974.
Buffs have been overhauled with Update 51, page needs to be updated

more.t: Put Major Breach on enemies to cut their physical and spell resistance by 5948 (value from the wiki Buffs page, which says it is not yet updated for Update 51).
q: Decrease target's physical and spell resistance by 5948.
Buffs have been overhauled with Update 51, page needs to be updated

more.t: Get penetration from [[The Lover]] mundus stone or Champion Point slottables such as Piercing.
more.q: Champion Point slottables, such as Piercing and Force of Nature.

more.t: Put Minor Brittle on enemies to raise their critical damage taken by 10% (wiki value that may predate the Update 51 buff overhaul).
q: Increases target's Crit Damage Taken by 10%
Buffs have been overhauled with Update 51, page needs to be updated

more.t: Deal Shock damage to Concuss enemies: they get Minor Vulnerability and take 5% more damage for 4 seconds.
q: The Concussion status can be applied by dealing Shock Damage to a target.
suffers from Minor Vulnerability for 4 seconds, increasing their damage taken by 5%

more.t: Deal Physical damage to Sunder enemies: they get Minor Breach for 4 seconds.
q: The Sundered status can be applied by dealing Physical Damage to a target.
suffers from Minor Breach debuff for 4 seconds

more.t: Know that damage-over-time abilities can apply a status effect on every tick.
more.q: Damage-over-time abilities have a chance to apply status effect on every tick of damage.

more.t: Cleanse debuffs with skills or items that have cleansing effects.
more.q: Debuffs can be removed by certain skills or items with cleansing effects.

more.t: Note that Malacath's Band of Brutality lowers your critical damage by 50%.
more.q: The mythic item Malacath's Band of Brutality decreases Critical Damage by 50%.

sections.title: How to tank in a group
sections.answer: Queue as Tank, wear heavy armor, taunt the boss with [[Puncture]] or [[Inner Fire]] and taunt it again before the taunt wears off.
sections.need: You'll need: a one-handed weapon and a shield for [[Puncture]], or the [[Undaunted]] skill line for [[Inner Fire]].

steps.t: Pick the **Tank** role in the Group & Activity Finder before you queue.
steps.q: The Role selection between Tank, Healer and Damage is now required, and is designed to create balanced groups for certain activities.

steps.t: Wear [[Heavy Armor]]: its skills are made for tanks, who need a lot of health.
steps.q: These skills generally aid "tank" characters— those who require a lot of health.

steps.t: Equip a one-handed weapon and a shield together.
steps.q: Use of these abilities, as well as progression through this skill line, requires equipping a one-handed weapon and a shield at the same time.

steps.t: Slot [[Puncture]] to taunt enemies in melee range.
steps.q: The Puncture skill in the One Hand and Shield line. This only works from melee range, and requires you to be wielding a one-handed weapon and shield.

steps.t: To taunt from a distance with any weapon, slot [[Inner Fire]] from the [[Undaunted]] line instead.
steps.q: The Inner Fire skill in the Undaunted line. This method works from a distance, and lets you use the equipment of your choice.

steps.t: Taunt the boss so it attacks you instead of your allies.
steps.q: It will cause the affected target to attack you instead of your allies.

steps.t: Taunt it again before 15 seconds pass, or the taunt wears off.
steps.q: After 15 seconds, the taunt will wear off, which can be disastrous in certain boss battles.

steps.t: Block an attack when yellow lines show it should be blocked.
steps.q: Note the yellow lines that indicate this attack should be blocked.

steps.t: Keep taunted enemies inside their area: taking one out of its leash zone resets the fight.
steps.q: Bringing a taunted enemy outside its leash zone will reset the fight.

steps.t: Cast [[Unstoppable]] with 5 pieces of heavy armor worn for Major Resolve and immunity to knockback.
q: Requires 5 pieces of heavy armor equipped Intensify your physical presence to gain Major Resolve
Also grants you immunity to knockback and disabling effects

sections.check: After your taunt the boss turns to you and keeps attacking you, not your group.

more.t: Other taunts: [[Destructive Clench]] (Frost Destruction Staff, ranged), [[Runic Jolt]] (Arcanist), [[Chains of Flame]] (Dragonknight) and [[Focused Charge]] (Templar).
q: The Destructive Clench skill with a Frost Destruction Staff provides a ranged taunt and immobilizes the target.
The Runic Jolt skill in the Arcanist's Soldier of Apocrypha line.
The Chains of Flame skill in the Dragonknight's Draconic Power line.
The Focused Charge skill in the Templar's Aedric Spear line.

more.t: Class lines for tanking: [[Draconic Power]] and [[Earthen Heart]] (Dragonknight), [[Bone Tyrant]] (Necromancer), [[Soldier of Apocrypha]] (Arcanist).
q: The Dragonknight class is best suited for tanking-oriented characters due to the Draconic Power and Earthen Heart skill lines
offering the Bone Tyrant skill line for tanking abilities
Soldier of Apocrypha for tanking abilities

more.t: Sets that taunt for you: [[Swarm Mother]] when you block, [[Tormentor]] when you use a Charge, Leap, Teleport or Pull ability.
q: Blocking attacks with the Swarm Mother set.
Using any Charge, Leap, Teleport, or Pull ability with the Tormentor set.

more.t: [[Undaunted Bastion]] gives you a damage shield when you taunt while below 75% Health.
more.q: The Undaunted Bastion set will give you a Damage Shield when taunting enemies while you're below 75% Health.

more.t: If you are not the tank, do not taunt: after one player taunts an enemy, another player cannot taunt it for 15 seconds.
q: When one player has taunted an enemy, another player may not taunt them for 15 seconds afterwards.
Generally speaking, if you are in a group and not playing the tank role, you should avoid using any kind of taunts.

more.t: An enemy nobody has taunted usually attacks the greatest damage threat.
more.q: If an enemy is not taunted, it will usually attack the greatest damage threat.

more.t: Two tanks can swap taunts: an enemy only becomes immune after more than five taunts from at least two players within 12 seconds.
more.q: These penalties have since been relaxed to be more than five taunts between at least two players in the same 12-second period.

more.t: In [[Kyne's Aegis]], face the Half-Giant Tidebreaker away from the group: it has a cleave attack.
more.q: Has a cleave attack, so tanks should make sure they are not facing towards the group.

upcoming.t: Coming with Update 52 (not live when this guide was checked): [[Unstoppable]] and its morphs taunt enemies around you, and [[Tormentor]] taunts every enemy hit, not only the first.
upcoming.q: The Unstoppable Heavy Armor skill and its morphs, as well as Goading Smash and Goading Vault, now offer an AoE Taunt. This makes it easier for Tanks to control groups of enemies and assist their allies. Additionally the Tormentor Set now taunts all enemies rather than only the first enemy hit

sections.title: How to heal in a group
sections.answer: Queue as Healer, equip a Restoration Staff, keep [[Regeneration]] and [[Grand Healing]] on your group, and heavy attack to get Magicka back.
sections.need: You'll need: a Restoration Staff.

steps.t: Pick the **Healer** role in the Group & Activity Finder before you queue.
steps.q: The Role selection between Tank, Healer and Damage is now required

steps.t: Equip a Restoration Staff: most of its skills heal and protect allies.
steps.q: Most active and passive abilities enabled by Restoration Staves focus on protecting and healing allies

steps.t: Kill an enemy with the staff equipped to unlock the [[Restoration Staff]] skill line.
steps.q: The Restoration Staff skill line is granted the first time you kill an enemy with a restoration staff equipped.

steps.t: Cast [[Regeneration]] on yourself or a hurt ally to heal them over time.
steps.q: Share your staff's life-giving energy, healing you or a nearby ally for

steps.t: Place [[Grand Healing]] under your group when several allies are hurt.
steps.q: Call upon restoring spirits with your staff, healing you and your allies in the target area for

steps.t: Cast [[Steadfast Ward]] to shield the ally with the lowest health.
steps.q: Call on your staff's strength to protect you or the lowest health ally around you with a damage shield

steps.t: Cast [[Blessing of Protection]] to heal the allies in front of you and give them Minor Resolve.
q: Slam your staff down to activate its blessings, healing you and your allies in front of you for
Also grants Minor Resolve

steps.t: Fully charge a heavy attack on an enemy to get Magicka back.
steps.q: dealing a fully-charged heavy attack to an enemy will also recharge the user's magicka based on their level

steps.t: Use the line's Ultimate, [[Panacea]], to heal you or an ally every 1 second for 5 seconds.
steps.q: healing you or an ally for [7687 / 7771 / 7856 / 7940] Health every 1 second for 5 seconds.

sections.check: Your group stays above half health between boss attacks and you still have Magicka left.

more.t: A heal in an area reaches at most 6 targets at a time.
more.q: Healing done in an area can only heal up to 6 targets at a time.

more.t: Class lines for healing: [[Green Balance]] (Warden), [[Living Death]] (Necromancer), [[Curative Runeforms]] (Arcanist).
q: Green Balance skill line for healing
Living Death for healing
Curative Runeforms for healing

more.t: [[Combat Prayer]], a morph of Blessing of Protection, also gives Minor Berserk: 5% more damage done for you and your allies.
more.q: Also grants Minor Berserk and Minor Resolve increasing you and your allies' damage done by 5%

more.t: [[Force Siphon]] puts Minor Lifesteal on an enemy: you and your allies heal while damaging it.
q: Focus your staff's power to apply Minor Lifesteal to an enemy for
healing you and your allies for 600 Health every 1 second when damaging them

more.t: Allies can use the synergies of your skills at no cost; each synergy has a 20 second cooldown per player.
q: Synergy activations cost no resources and are independent of skill cooldowns.
Synergies have a 20 second cooldown per player for each individual Synergy.

more.t: The current update's patch notes cut back the group healing of Strife and Funnel so those skills do not replace healers.
more.q: we’re also gently peeling back the group healing of Strife and Funnel to account for this, to try and avoid cases where these abilities replace healers in group scenarios.

more.t: In [[Kyne's Aegis]], the hardest add pulls need the healers to slot [[Inner Fire]] and taunt some adds.
more.q: To do this pull effectively you will need to have the Healers run Inner Fire to taunt certain adds.

sections.title: How to run group dungeons
sections.answer: Group up to four players, queue or travel to a dungeon, and take daily Undaunted pledges for keys.
sections.need: You'll need: a group of up to four players, or the Dungeon Finder.

steps.t: Form a group of up to four players.
steps.q: Group Dungeons are designed to be explored with a group of four players maximum.

steps.t: If you are under level 50, enter through the Dungeon Finder to get the Looking for Group buff.
steps.q: Entering a group dungeon through the Dungeon Finder while under level 50 will give you the "Looking for Group" buff

steps.t: Talk to the Undaunted in a major city tavern to add dungeons to your map.
steps.q: They can be added to your map by talking to members of the Undaunted in the taverns of the major cities of each zone

steps.t: Run a random dungeon from the dungeon finder for Premium Undaunted Exploration Supplies once every 20 hours.
steps.q: Completing the Daily event will grant Premium Undaunted Exploration Supplies. This event has a 20 hour cooldown per character

steps.t: At level 45, open the Undaunted Enclave Invitation from your mail.
steps.q: open the "Undaunted Enclave Invitation" item that you receive in the mail upon reaching level 45

steps.t: Sign the Tome of the Undaunted in your capital city.
steps.q: It will begin a prerequisite quest for you to sign the "Tome of the Undaunted" in your capital city.

steps.t: Take up to three pledges a day, one from each Pledge Master.
steps.q: It is possible to complete up to three pledges per character per day, a different one offered by each of the three Pledge Masters at the enclave.

steps.t: If you do not own the DLC dungeons, take pledges only from Maj and Glirion.
steps.q: players without access to the DLCs can easily avoid them by only getting pledges from Maj and Glirion.

steps.t: Reach level 50 to unlock Veteran dungeons.
steps.q: These can be accessed once you hit Level 50 and unlock Veteran content.

steps.t: Read the Scroll of Glorious Battle near the last boss to turn on Hard Mode.
steps.q: it is activated by a member of the group reading the glowing "Scroll of Glorious Battle" that can be found on the floor near the dungeon's last boss arena.

steps.t: Clear Hard Mode with a pledge active to get two Undaunted Keys instead of one.
steps.q: Completing a dungeon in Hard Mode grants an achievement and, if an Undaunted Pledge is active, two Undaunted Keys instead of one.

steps.t: Spend your keys at any Pledge Master in the Undaunted enclave.
steps.q: Each key can be spent at any of the Pledge Masters at the Undaunted enclave.

sections.check: Your pledge quest completes and you get a key to spend at the Pledge Masters.

more.t: The Looking for Group buff gives 25% more Max Health and 20% more Weapon and Spell Damage.
more.q: increases your Max Health by 25% and your Weapon and Spell Damage by 20%

more.t: Expect DLC dungeons to need level 45 even on normal.
more.q: All DLC dungeons on normal difficulty have a minimum character requirement of level 45.

more.t: Do DLC pledges for more keys: two, three or four for normal, veteran or veteran hard mode.
more.q: DLC dungeon pledges reward you with two, three or four keys for normal, veteran or veteran hard mode respectively.

more.t: Plan on at most eight keys per character per day.
more.q: The maximum number of keys that can be earned in a day per character is thus eight.

more.t: Look for Challenge Banners in newer dungeons: they replace the scroll and keep Hard Mode on between attempts.
more.q: banners preserve their state between attempts, without having to reactivate them every time

more.t: Collect each dungeon's own gear sets.
more.q: Each dungeon also has associated collectible gear sets.

more.t: Expect veteran mode to give better loot.
more.q: They are understandably much more difficult, but earn you higher-quality loot and Veteran Dungeon Achievements.

sections.title: How to start doing trials
sections.answer: Join a group of 12, start on Normal mode, and claim each trial's reward coffer once a week.
sections.need: You'll need: a group of 12 players.

steps.t: Find a group of 12 players.
steps.q: They are designed for groups of 12, and each has a leaderboard associated with it.

steps.t: Start on Normal mode, the easier mode.
steps.q: They remain challenging dungeon instances geared towards groups of twelve players, although they now have an easier Normal mode.

steps.t: If you own no DLC, start with [[Aetherian Archive]], [[Hel Ra Citadel]] or [[Sanctum Ophidia]]: they are in the base game.
steps.q: Trials: Aetherian Archive, Hel Ra Citadel, and Sanctum Ophidia are included in the base game.

steps.t: Play [[Halls of Fabrication]] too: it has been free since April 2022.
steps.q: Halls of Fabrication has been free since April 2022.

steps.t: Play [[Kyne's Aegis]] in [[Western Skyrim]] too: Greymoor joined the base game with Season Two on 21 October 2026.
q: Greymoor: Western Skyrim and Blackreach: Greymoor Caverns (integrated to the base game with the launch of Season Two on 21 October 2026)
Haafingar, Western Skyrim

steps.t: Play [[Maw of Lorkhaj]] too: it needs the Thieves Guild DLC, which joined the base game in March 2026.
q: Even though this trial is in an Alliance Zone region, access to the Thieves Guild DLC is required to run it.
Thieves Guild: Hew's Bane (integrated into the base game since March 2026)

steps.t: Claim each trial's reward coffer once per week.
steps.q: You can only earn the reward coffer from each trial quest once per week.

steps.t: If you play on the North American server, plan for the week to start Tuesday 6am ET (10am UTC).
steps.q: on the North American server, the weekly coffer and the trial of the week quest period begins on Tuesday 6am ET (10am UTC)

steps.t: If you play on the European server, plan for the week to start Tuesday 3am UTC.
steps.q: on the European server, the period begins on Tuesday 3am UTC (Monday 11pm ET)

steps.t: Reach level 50 to unlock Veteran trials.
q: Veteran content in the Elder Scrolls Online is unlocked when a character reaches Level 50.
Similarly, Veteran Trials and Arenas also become available, and offer access to leaderboards, increased rewards, and new achievements.

steps.t: Run Veteran mode for perfected trial sets.
steps.q: Perfected versions of trial and arena sets only drop in Veteran mode.

steps.t: Turn on Hard Mode by using the item or object near certain bosses.
q: Trials also have an additional Hard Mode for certain bosses, which can be activated manually within the dungeon itself.
It typically involves activating an item or an object found near the boss.

steps.t: Switch Hard Mode on or off as you like, except in the [[Craglorn]] trials.
steps.q: Trials hard mode can be turned on and off in all trials except for those in Craglorn.

steps.t: Check which trial is the weekly trial for the leaderboards.
steps.q: Each week, a random trial is chosen as the weekly trial for the leaderboards.

sections.check: After the final boss you get the weekly reward coffer for that trial.

more.t: Find [[Aetherian Archive]], [[Hel Ra Citadel]] and [[Sanctum Ophidia]] in [[Craglorn]].
q: Aetherian Archive — A tower in southeastern Craglorn near the city of Elinhir.
Hel Ra Citadel — An ancient Yokudan fortress in southwestern Craglorn.
Sanctum Ophidia — An ancient Nedic temple in northern Craglorn.

more.t: Find [[Halls of Fabrication]] in [[Vvardenfell]] and the mini trial [[Asylum Sanctorium]] in [[Clockwork City]].
q: Halls of Fabrication — A part of Sotha Sil's Clockwork City.
Asylum Sanctorium — A mini trial found within the Reactor District in the Brass Fortress.

more.t: Find [[Maw of Lorkhaj]] in [[Reaper's March]], [[Cloudrest]] in [[Summerset]] and [[Sunspire]] in [[Northern Elsweyr]].
q: Maw of Lorkhaj — A desecrated Khajiiti temple in Reaper's March.
Cloudrest — A city found on the mountain of Eton Nir in Summerset, east of Ebon Stadmont.
Sunspire — An ancient temple of Alkosh found in Northern Elsweyr.

more.t: Find [[Kyne's Aegis]] in [[Western Skyrim]], [[Rockgrove]] in [[Blackwood]] and [[Dreadsail Reef]] in [[High Isle]].
q: Kyne's Aegis — A bastion in the Sea of Ghosts, located on an island off the coast north of Solitude.
Rockgrove — An Argonian settlement and trial located in the southeastern reaches of Blackwood.
Dreadsail Reef — A reef off the coast of High Isle that serves as a major base for the Dreadsails

more.t: Find [[Sanity's Edge]] in [[Telvanni Peninsula]], [[Lucent Citadel]] from [[West Weald]] and [[Ossein Cage]] from [[Solstice]].
q: Sanity's Edge — The dreamworld of Warlock Vanton.
Lucent Citadel — A ruined stronghold in the wastelands of Fargrave, accessible from West Weald.
Ossein Cage — A Coldharbour prison that is accessible from Solstice.

more.t: Find [[Opulent Ordeal]] in the Night Market event zone; it is not part of the weekly trial.
q: Opulent Ordeal — A trial created by the enigmatic Opulent entities of the Night Market to test newcomers.
This does not apply to the Opulent Ordeal, as it is located within an Event Zone.

sections.title: How to get stronger solo (arenas, solo dungeons, Infinite Archive)
sections.answer: Train in the solo arenas, the Wolfhunter solo dungeons and the Infinite Archive.
sections.need: You'll need: a character that can fight alone, or a companion.

steps.t: Enter Maelstrom Arena from [[Wrothgar]] for a solo arena.
steps.q: Maelstrom Arena — An otherworldly solo arena accessed from Wrothgar.

steps.t: Enter [[Vateshran Hollows]] in [[The Reach]] for another solo arena.
steps.q: Vateshran Hollows — A solo arena in the Reach, south of the Reachwind Ritual Site.

steps.t: Use Sigils in Normal mode; skip them in Veteran mode if you want a higher leaderboard score.
steps.q: In Normal mode, use of these synergies is encouraged, but in Veteran mode the use of a Sigil will reduce your final overall leaderboard score.

steps.t: Run the solo versions of [[March of Sacrifices]] or [[Moon Hunter Keep]], alone or with a companion.
q: Solo Dungeons are instanced PvE content, balanced around a Solo player and optionally a Companion.
collected from the March of Sacrifices and Moon Hunter Keep solo dungeons

steps.t: Pick 1 to 3 Meted Misfortunes at the start to set the difficulty and rewards.
q: Meted Misfortunes are a mechanic unique to the Solo Dungeons, which control the difficulty level and rewards the dungeon will have.
you can pick between 1-3 of them

steps.t: Pick Veteran or Dauntless difficulty for a guaranteed Monster Mask set piece.
steps.q: Guaranteed Monster Mask item set piece and [Associated Dungeon Bust]

steps.t: Trade your Undaunted Crests to the Crest Merchant Veya Thenim.
steps.q: Solo Dungeons will also provide a unique currency, Undaunted Crests which can be traded to the Crest Merchant Veya Thenim for items.

steps.t: Travel to the [[Infinite Archive]] with its icon on the [[Apocrypha]] map.
steps.q: it can be accessed by clicking on the icon on the Apocrypha map and teleporting directly to the Archive

steps.t: Enter solo, with a companion, or with one friend.
steps.q: Players may enter solo, with an NPC Companion, or with one friend (in a duo).

steps.t: Clear all three waves of a round without dying.
steps.q: You must complete all three waves without dying to complete the round.

steps.t: Guard your Threads: each death in the Archive costs one.
steps.q: If you are killed by any means in the archive, you will lose one of these Threads.

steps.t: Pick a Verse at the end of each Stage; it lasts until the end of the next Stage.
steps.q: Verses are temporary buffs that last until the end of the next Stage.

sections.check: Your Infinite Archive run reaches later Cycles and Arcs, and your solo dungeon clears drop Monster Mask pieces.

more.t: You start the Archive with three Threads.
more.q: When you first enter the Archive, you will have three Threads available

more.t: Use the hourglass at the dungeon start to reset your Misfortunes.
more.q: use the hourglass found at the start of the dungeon to reset them.

more.t: Pick a Vision at the end of each Cycle; it stays until you finish the Archive.
q: At the end of each Cycle (including the 5th Cycle where you face Tho'at), you will be given a choice between 2 random Visions
Visions are enduring buffs that will be on your character until you finish the Infinite Archive.

more.t: Spend Archival Fortunes at the merchants at the Archive entrance.
more.q: Archival Fortunes can be spent at the merchants in the entrance area of the Infinite Archive in return for special rewards

more.t: Play the Infinite Archive without a chapter: it is part of the base game.
more.q: The Infinite Archive is part of the base game and is accessible for all players, regardless of ESO Plus subscription or ownership of the Necrom Chapter.

more.t: Buy class set pieces from Filer Brax in the Archive Index Hall.
more.q: Filer Brax offers class set pieces and is always available in the Archive Index Hall.

more.t: Play the solo dungeons free: Wolfhunter was made free on October 19, 2026.
more.q: On October 19, 2026, the Wolfhunter Dungeon DLC was made free for all players as its dungeons were given Solo versions.

more.t: [[Vateshran Hollows]] needs no DLC now: [[The Reach]] joined the base game with Markarth on 9 November 2026.
q: Vateshran Hollows — A solo arena in the Reach, south of the Reachwind Ritual Site.
Markarth: The Reach and Blackreach: Arkthzand Cavern (added to the base game on 9 November 2026)

sections.title: About zones and chapter order
sections.answer: Each alliance has its own zones, all zones scale to you, and the chapters came out from Morrowind to Gold Road.
sections.need: You'll need: nothing; this explains how the world is laid out.

paras.t: The base-game zones are split by alliance: five per alliance, plus one or two starter zones.
paras.q: The base-game zones are divided by Alliance, with five to each Alliance as well as one or two starter zones

paras.t: Aldmeri Dominion zones: [[Auridon]], [[Grahtwood]], [[Greenshade]], [[Khenarthi's Roost]], [[Malabal Tor]] and [[Reaper's March]].
paras.q: Aldmeri Dominion: Auridon, Grahtwood, Greenshade, Khenarthi's Roost, Malabal Tor, Reaper's March

paras.t: Daggerfall Covenant zones: [[Alik'r Desert]], [[Bangkorai]], [[Betnikh]], [[Glenumbra]], [[Rivenspire]], [[Stormhaven]] and [[Stros M'Kai]].
paras.q: Daggerfall Covenant: Alik'r Desert, Bangkorai, Betnikh, Glenumbra, Rivenspire, Stormhaven, Stros M'Kai

paras.t: Ebonheart Pact zones: [[Bal Foyen]], [[Bleakrock Isle]], [[Deshaan]], [[Eastmarch]], [[The Rift]], [[Shadowfen]] and [[Stonefalls]].
paras.q: Ebonheart Pact: Bal Foyen, Bleakrock Isle, Deshaan, Eastmarch, The Rift, Shadowfen, Stonefalls

paras.t: All zones now scale with Battle Leveling; the zone order still matters for the story.
paras.q: The tiered ordering of zones remains important for story progression, but the level banding no longer exists, as all zones are subject to the Battle Leveling system

paras.t: [[Cyrodiil]] is one large zone split into three disputed territories.
paras.q: Cyrodiil is one zone, much larger than the others, divided into three larger-than-normal disputed territories.

paras.t: The main quest starts with Soul Shriven in Coldharbour, where you escape from [[Coldharbour]].
paras.q: Soul Shriven in Coldharbour: Escape from the depths of Coldharbour.

paras.t: The first four Chapters: Morrowind (2017, [[Vvardenfell]]), Summerset (2018), Elsweyr (2019, [[Northern Elsweyr]]) and Greymoor ([[Western Skyrim]]).
q: Morrowind is the first Chapter of The Elder Scrolls Online. It is an expansion set on the island of Vvardenfell.
officially launched on all platforms on June 6, 2017
Summerset is the second Chapter of The Elder Scrolls Online.
21 May 2018 (early access) 5 June 2018
Elsweyr is the third Chapter of The Elder Scrolls Online. It is an expansion set in Northern Elsweyr.
20 May 2019 (early access) 4 June 2019
Greymoor is the fourth Chapter of The Elder Scrolls Online. Supernatural harrowstorms plague Western Skyrim

paras.t: The next four Chapters: Blackwood, High Isle, Necrom ([[Telvanni Peninsula]], with the [[Arcanist]] class) and Gold Road (2024, [[West Weald]]).
q: Blackwood is the fifth Chapter of The Elder Scrolls Online.
High Isle is the sixth Chapter of The Elder Scrolls Online.
Necrom is the seventh Chapter of The Elder Scrolls Online. It is an expansion set on the Telvanni Peninsula
It also includes the new Arcanist class.
The expansion is set in the Colovian region of the West Weald, and was released on June 3, 2024 for PC/Mac

paras.t: Chapters were put aside in 2025 in favor of Seasons; the first, Season Zero, was released on April 2, 2026.
q: As of 2025, Chapters have been "put aside" in favor of a new content delivery system referred to as Seasons
Season Zero: Dawn and Dusk — Introduces the Night Market event zone
Released April 2, 2026

paras.t: Greymoor's [[Western Skyrim]] and [[Blackreach: Greymoor Caverns]] joined the base game with Season Two on 21 October 2026.
paras.q: Greymoor: Western Skyrim and Blackreach: Greymoor Caverns (integrated to the base game with the launch of Season Two on 21 October 2026)

paras.t: Markarth joined the base game in Update 51 Incremental 2, adding [[The Reach]] and [[Blackreach: Arkthzand Cavern]]; you get it on your first login.
q: Players who do not own this DLC will receive it upon their first login after Update 51 Incremental 2 is live.
Markarth: The Reach and Blackreach: Arkthzand Cavern (added to the base game on 9 November 2026)

sections.check: Your Collections menu shows the DLC and zones your account owns.

more.t: Morrowind's [[Vvardenfell]] has been fully part of the base game since March 2026.
more.q: Morrowind: Vvardenfell (available for free since April 2022, and fully integrated into the base game since March 2026)

more.t: The [[Warden]] class joined the base game with Update 49 in early March 2026.
more.q: The Warden class was added to the base game with the launch of Update 49 on 6 March 2026

more.t: ESO Plus members can use all DLC while subscribed.
more.q: ESO Plus members are given access to all DLC for the duration of their subscription.

more.t: Check what your account owns in the Collections menu.
more.q: to see what content is owned on your account, visit the Collections Menu and visit the Collectibles, Stories, etc. tabs.

sections.title: How to start PvP
sections.answer: Go to Cyrodiil from level 10 for the Alliance War, or queue Battlegrounds through the Group & Activity Finder.
sections.need: You'll need: a character of level 10 or higher.

steps.t: Reach level 10 to join a campaign in [[Cyrodiil]].
steps.q: At Level 10, you will be able to go to Cyrodiil and start participating in a Campaign.

steps.t: Choose one campaign as your Home Campaign.
steps.q: A player can choose one campaign as their "Home Campaign."

steps.t: Do the tutorial quest Welcome to Cyrodiil to become a Volunteer.
steps.q: by completing the tutorial quest Welcome to Cyrodiil, you will become enlisted as a Volunteer

steps.t: Go in at any level: battle leveling scales up your attributes, armor and damage.
q: Every player who enters Cyrodiil is given the Battle Spirit bonus, regardless of their level.
which scales up their attributes, armor, and damage ratings in order to remain competitive

steps.t: Take repeatable quests from your alliance general to learn how to capture keeps.
steps.q: Each alliance general offers a range of repeatable quests designed to direct players through the motions of capturing a keep or resource.

steps.t: Earn Alliance Points to rank up; each rank gives one skill point.
q: As you gain Alliance Points, you will increase your Alliance War Rank further
Each rank gained will reward you with one skill point.

steps.t: Queue Battlegrounds through the **Group & Activity Finder**.
steps.q: Battlegrounds are small-scale player-versus-player (PvP) gameplay locations that can be accessed through the Group & Activity Finder.

steps.t: Queue alone or with a pre-formed group.
steps.q: you are able to queue up for Battlegrounds individually or in pre-formed groups

steps.t: Win your first battleground of the day for a Competitive Reward Box.
steps.q: You get a Battlemaster Rivyn's Competitive Reward Box by winning your first battleground of the day

sections.check: Your Alliance War rank goes up as you earn Alliance Points.

more.t: Crown an Emperor by taking all six keeps around the Imperial City.
more.q: By capturing all six of the keeps surrounding the Imperial City, your alliance will have the opportunity to crown a player as Emperor.

more.t: Expect your Battlegrounds team to be random, not your alliance.
more.q: Your team is assigned randomly on entering each Battleground

glossary.note: Short meanings for words a returning player meets. Each one quotes a cached UESP page; build.py checks every quote and number.

terms.t: Points you earn with experience after level 50. They let you wear stronger gear and use stronger consumables up to CP 160.
q: Gaining Champion Points allows players to equip more powerful gear and use more powerful consumables, up to the Champion Progression Cap of 160.
The Champion System is unlocked when one of your characters reaches Veteran rank at Level 50.

terms.t: The harder version of content, open once you reach the maximum level.
terms.q: Upon reaching the maximum level, players unlock Veteran content and receive 10 points into the Champion system.

terms.t: Swapping up to two of your class skill lines for lines from other classes.
terms.q: It allows a player to customize their character by replacing up to two of their class' skill lines with those from other classes.

terms.t: Passive skill lines for each class, added in Update 50.
terms.q: Class Mastery is a skill system introduced with Update 50 that provides passive skill lines for each of the seven Player Classes.

terms.t: An active skill that reached rank 4 can be morphed into one of two new versions.
terms.q: They have 4 Ranks, after which they may be Morphed into a new version.

terms.t: A third resource, used by Ultimate skills instead of Magicka or Stamina.
terms.q: Ultimate Skills are similar to Active Skills, but instead of using Stamina or Magicka as most Active Skills do, these use a third resource called Ultimate.

terms.t: A special ability your allies can activate when you use certain skills or sets.
terms.q: Synergies are special abilities that other allied players may activate when you use certain skills or sets.

terms.t: The state an enemy enters when you block its heavy attack; a heavy attack on it then knocks it down for 70% more damage.
q: Blocking an enemy's heavy attack will set it Off Balance.
Using a heavy attack against an Off Balance opponent will knock them down, deal 70% more damage and restore double the resources.

terms.t: How much of your damage breaks through an enemy's armor.
terms.q: Penetration is a value that represents how much of your damage will break through an opponent's armor.

terms.t: A standing stone that gives one permanent blessing at a time.
terms.q: Mundus Stones are standing stones dedicated to the Constellations.

terms.t: A two-piece set (head and shoulders) named after a dungeon boss.
terms.q: Monster Helm Sets (commonly called "monster heads") are a subset of dungeon sets of armor.

terms.t: A one-piece set you build from Antiquities leads.
terms.q: Mythic Items are special one-piece sets that can only be obtained through the Antiquities system and if you have access to the related DLC.

terms.t: The stronger version of a trial or arena set, dropped only on Veteran.
terms.q: Perfected versions of trial and arena sets only drop in Veteran mode.

terms.t: An optional harder fight on the last boss of a Veteran dungeon.
terms.q: For an even greater challenge, Veteran Dungeons have an optional Death Challenge (more commonly called "Hard Mode") that can be activated on the last boss.

terms.t: A daily Undaunted quest to clear a group dungeon, open from level 45.
terms.q: Undaunted Pledges are Daily Quests which become available at Level 45 from the Undaunted Enclave in your Alliance Capital

terms.t: The currency you spend to change an item's trait to one you have researched.
terms.q: 50 Transmute Crystals are used to change the traits of armor and weapons to a trait previously researched for that item.

terms.t: A collectible found around the world; collecting them gives skill points.
terms.q: Skyshards are collectible items that can be found throughout the world.

terms.t: An activity and rewards system added in Update 44.
terms.q: Golden Pursuits is an activity and rewards system introduced with Update 44.

terms.t: A battle pass-style reward system.
terms.q: Tamriel Tomes is a battle pass-style reward system for Elder Scrolls Online.

terms.t: Scaling that raises a lower-level player's attributes, armor and damage so they stay competitive.
terms.q: this also stacks with "battle leveling", which scales up their attributes, armor, and damage ratings in order to remain competitive.

terms.t: Debuffs you pick at the start of a solo dungeon; they set its difficulty and rewards.
terms.q: Meted Misfortunes are a mechanic unique to the Solo Dungeons, which control the difficulty level and rewards the dungeon will have.

terms.t: In the Infinite Archive you start with three Threads (lives); Verses are temporary buffs that last until the end of the next Stage.
q: When you first enter the Archive, you will have three Threads available
Verses are temporary buffs that last until the end of the next Stage.

terms.t: Synergies that appear at the start of each round in most arenas.
terms.q: A core mechanic of most Arenas is the presence of Sigils, synergies that appear at the beginning of each round of combat.

terms.t: While Enlightened you earn experience four times faster toward Champion Points; you get 400,000 XP of it per day.
q: While you are Enlightened, experience gain is multiplied by four
Once per day, you receive 400,000 XP of Enlightenment

terms.t: An armor trait that makes your Mundus Stone stronger.
terms.q: Armor with the Divines Trait increases the effect of Mundus Stones, depending on the Armor's quality.

terms.t: What crafting professions use to level up.
terms.q: All seven crafting professions use Inspiration for leveling purposes.

terms.t: Ingredients used to improve a crafted piece further.
terms.q: the piece can be augmented even more through the use of tempers.

bonuses.t: When you use an Ultimate ability, you heal for 51 Health and restore 51 Stamina and Magicka per Ultimate spent.

sets.name: Wizard's Riposte
sets.where: Wizard's Riposte is an Battlegrounds Set rewarded by Battlegrounds.

bonuses.t:
Adds 660 Critical Resistance
When you take direct Critical Damage, you apply Minor Enervation to the enemy for 5 seconds, reducing their Critical Damage done by 10%.

sets.name: Wrath of Elements
sets.where: Wrath of Elements is a Vateshran Weapons item set which drops in normal Vateshran Hollows.

bonuses.t: Casting Weakness to Elements on a target within 15 meters of you causes a surge of elemental energy to tether between you for 10 seconds. While the tether persists, enemies touching the tether take 331 Flame Damage, 331 Shock Damage, or 331 Frost Damage every 1 second, which increases by 1% each time it deals damage, up to 20%. This effect can occur once every 10 seconds, and scales off the higher of your Weapon and Spell Damage.

sets.name: Wrath of the Imperium
sets.where: Wrath of the Imperium is an item set found in boxes purchased using Alliance Points from the Cropsford Quartermaster, as quest rewards in Cropsford, as a reward for completing delves and dolmens throughout Cyrodiil, from completing Board Missions, and from Elite Gear Vendors.

bonuses.t: Adds 325 Weapon and Spell Damage to your ranged direct damage abilities.

sets.name: Wrathsun
sets.where: Wrathsun is a Class set found in the Infinite Archive.

bonuses.t: When you deal damage with a Dawn's Wrath ability, you gain a stack of Sunlight for 15 seconds, once per attack and up to 30 times. Each stack grants 21 Magicka Recovery. When at max stacks, stacks no longer refresh, your Templar skill line abilities deal 25% bonus damage but is reduced to 10% against players, and a Wrathful Nova is cast on the enemy. When Sunlight expires at max stacks, you lose 50% of your current Magicka.

sets.name: Wretched Vitality
sets.where: Crafted at Stormwright's Cleft in the Deadlands. You need three traits researched on the item.

bonuses.t: While in combat, applying a Major Buff or Debuff with a duration to a target grants you 260 Magicka and Stamina Recovery for 15 seconds. While in combat, applying a Minor Buff or Debuff with a duration to a target grants you 130 Magicka and Stamina Recovery for 15 seconds.

sets.name: Wyrd Tree's Blessing
sets.where: Wyrd Tree's Blessing is an overland set that drops in Glenumbra.

bonuses.t: When you cast a Magicka ability, you remove all negative effects from yourself. This effect can occur once every 15 seconds.

sets.name: Xanmeer Genesis
sets.where: Xanmeer Genesis is an overland set that drops in Solstice.

bonuses.t: When an enemy you have recently damaged dies, after 0.5 seconds, you and allies within 8 meters of the dead enemy receive 322 Health, Magicka, and Stamina Recovery for 10 seconds. This effect can occur once every 6 seconds.

sets.name: Xanmeer Spellweaver
sets.where: Xanmeer Spellweaver is a dungeon set that drops in Naj-Caldeesh.

bonuses.t: Increase your damage done with Flame, Frost, and Shock Damage by 5%. Increase your damage done with Burning, Chilled, and Concussion by an additional 15%.

sets.name: Xoryn's Masterpiece
sets.where: Xoryn's Masterpiece is a trial set found in normal Lucent Citadel.

bonuses.t: Gain Minor Aegis, reducing damage taken from monsters by 5%.
Increases Max Magicka and Max Stamina by 1667 for you and up to 11 other group members within 28 meters of you. This bonus persists through death.

sets.name: Yandir's Might
sets.where: Yandir's Might is a trial set which drops in normal Kyne's Aegis.

bonuses.t: Gain Minor Slayer, increasing damage done to monsters by 5%.

Dealing Critical Damage increases your Weapon and Spell Damage by 86, stacking up to 5 times. This effect can occur once every 0.5 seconds. Completing a fully-charged Heavy Attack removes all stacks and increases your Weapon and Spell Damage by 136 per stack removed. You cannot have both effects active at the same time.

sets.name: Ysgramor's Birthright
sets.where: Ysgramor's Birthright is an overland set that drops in The Rift.

bonuses.t: Adds 400 Weapon and Spell Damage to your Frost Damage abilities.

sets.name: Z'en's Redress
sets.where: Z'en's Redress is a dungeon set that drops in the Lair of Maarselok.

bonuses.t: Your Light Attacks apply the Touch of Z'en on enemies for 20 seconds. Enemies with the Touch of Z'en take an additional 1% more damage for each damage over time effect you've placed on them, up to 5%. Enemies can only be affected by one Touch of Z'en at a time.

sets.name: Zaan
sets.where: Zaan is a monster helm set. It drops in Scalecaller Peak.
drops: The head drops from Zaan the Scalecaller in Veteran Scalecaller Peak.
The shoulders can be obtained from Urgarlag Chief-bane's reward chest at Undaunted Enclaves.

bonuses.t: When you deal Critical Damage with a Light or Heavy Attack, you have a 33% chance to tether to your enemy for 10 seconds as long as you remain within 8 meters of them. Enemies touching the tether take 145 Flame damage every 1 second, increasing by 100% per tick and are afflicted with the Burning status effect. This effect can occur once every 20 seconds and scales off the higher of your Weapon and Spell Damage.

sets.name: Zoal the Ever-Wakeful
sets.where: Zoal the Ever-Wakeful is a monster helm set.
drops: The head drops from Zoal the Ever-Wakeful in the Imperial City Elven Gardens District.
The shoulders can be obtained from the Tel Var grand armorer in your alliance sewer headquarters for or from the vendor in the Planar Armor Trophy Vault.

bonuses.t: When you Break Free, you release a wave of Watcher energy, causing enemies within 8 meters of you to become Feared for 3 seconds. You also gain 34 Weapon and Spell Damage for each enemy hit, up to 6 enemies, for 7 seconds.

balanced-warrior.name: Balanced Warrior
balanced-warrior.desc: Increases your Armor for each Templar ability slotted. Increases your Weapon and Spell Damage based on your total Armor and number of Templar abilities slotted. 1% Armor 38 Weapon and Spell Damage
balanced-warrior.desc_max: Increases your Armor for each Templar ability slotted. Increases your Weapon and Spell Damage based on your total Armor and number of Templar abilities slotted. 2% Armor 78 Weapon and Spell Damage

assassins-blade.name: Assassin's Blade
assassins-blade.desc: Thrust a magic blade with lethal precision to stab an enemy, dealing 3175 Magic Damage. Deals 300% more damage to enemies below 25% Health.

morphs.name: Killer's Blade
morphs.note: Converts into a Stamina ability, deals Disease Damage, and now scales linearly based on missing Health rather than a flat value. Also heals you if the target dies within two seconds of use.
morphs.desc:
Cost: 2066 Stamina.
Thrust a caustic blade with lethal precision to stab an enemy, dealing 3175 Disease Damage. Deals up to 400% more damage to enemies with less than 50% Health. Heals you for 6558 if the enemy dies within 2 seconds of being struck.

morphs.name: Impale
morphs.note: Allows you to use the ability at range and increases the execute multiplier.
morphs.desc:
Range: 28 meters.
Throw a magic blade with lethal precision to strike an enemy, dealing 3175 Magic Damage. Deals 330% more damage to enemies below 25% Health.

blur.name: Blur
blur.desc:
Duration: 20 seconds.
Surround yourself in a phantasmic aura to gain Major Evasion, reducing damage from area attacks by 20% for 20 seconds. While active, taking direct damage reduces the cost of your next Roll Dodge by 10%, up to a maximum of 100%. This effect can stack up to once every half second.

morphs.name: Mirage
morphs.note: Grants Minor Resolve, increasing your Physical and Spell Resistance. Reduces the cost as the ability ranks up.
morphs.desc:
Cost: 3510 Magicka.
Surround yourself in a phantasmic aura to gain Major Evasion and Minor Resolve, reducing damage from area attacks by 20% and increasing your Physical and Spell Resistance by 2974 for 20 seconds. While active, taking direct damage reduces the cost of your next Roll Dodge by 10%, up to a maximum of 100%. This effect can stack up to once every half second.

morphs.name: Phantasmal Escape
morphs.note: Grants snare and immobilization immunity for a short duration.
morphs.desc: Surround yourself in a phantasmic aura to gain Major Evasion, reducing damage from area attacks by 20% for 20 seconds. Activating this ability removes all snares and immobilizations from you and grants immunity to them for 4 seconds. While active, taking direct damage reduces the cost of your next Roll Dodge by 10%, up to a maximum of 100%. This effect can stack up to once every half second.

blood-magic.name: Blood Magic
blood-magic.desc: When you cast a Dark Magic ability with a cost, you heal for 480 Health if you are not at full Health. This portion of the ability scales off your Max Health. If your Health is full, the higher of your Max Magicka or Stamina is increased by 5% for 10 seconds.
blood-magic.desc_max: When you cast a Dark Magic ability with a cost, you heal for 960 Health if you are not at full Health. This portion of the ability scales off your Max Health. If your Health is full, the higher of your Max Magicka or Stamina is increased by 10% for 10 seconds.

backlash.name: Backlash
backlash.desc: Bring forth an expanding beam of pure sunlight to doom an enemy, dealing 3172 Magic Damage immediately and marking them for 6 seconds. After the duration ends, the sunlight bursts, dealing 3513 Magic Damage to the enemy, which increases based on the amount of damage you dealt to them over the duration, up to 200%. You can have only one Backlash active at a time.

morphs.name: Purifying Light
morphs.note: When the effect ends, a pool of sunlight remains attached to the enemy, healing you and allies.
morphs.desc: Bring forth an expanding beam of pure sunlight to doom an enemy, dealing 3174 Magic Damage while marking them for 6 seconds. After the duration ends, the sunlight bursts, dealing 3512 Magic Damage, which increases based on the amount of damage you dealt to them over the duration, up to 200%. Also heals you and nearby allies in the area for 1639 Health every 2 seconds, over 10 seconds. You can have only one Purifying Light at a time.

morphs.name: Power of the Light
morphs.note: Converts into a Stamina ability, deals Physical Damage, and always applies the Sundered status effect.
morphs.desc:
Cost: 1337 Stamina.
Bring forth an expanding beam of pure sunlight to doom an enemy, dealing 3174 Physical Damage immediately and marking them for 6 seconds. After the duration ends, the sunlight bursts, dealing 3512 Physical Damage to the enemy, which increases based on the amount of damage you dealt to them over the duration, up to 200%. You can have only one Power of the Light active at a time, and each hit of the ability applies the Sundered status effect.

ancient-knowledge.name: Ancient Knowledge
ancient-knowledge.desc: With Destruction Staff Equipped Inferno Staves increases your damage done with damage over time and Status Effects by 6%. Lightning Staves increases your damage done with direct damage and channeled effects by 6%. Ice Staves reduce the cost of blocking by 18% and increases the amount of damage you block by 10%.
ancient-knowledge.desc_max: With Destruction Staff Equipped Inferno Staves increases your damage done with damage over time and Status Effects by 12%. Lightning Staves increases your damage done with direct damage and channeled effects by 12%. Equipping an Ice Staff reduces the cost of blocking by 36% and increases the amount of damage you block by 20%.

banish-the-wicked.name: Banish the Wicked
banish-the-wicked.desc: WITH A FIGHTERS GUILD ABILITY SLOTTED You generate 1 Ultimate whenever you kill an enemy.
banish-the-wicked.desc_max: WITH A FIGHTERS GUILD ABILITY SLOTTED You generate 3 Ultimate whenever you kill an enemy.

annulment.name: Annulment
annulment.desc: Requires 5 pieces of light armor equipped Convert a portion of your Magicka into a protective ward, gaining a damage shield that absorbs 9297 damage for 6 seconds. Damage shield strength capped at 50% of your Max Health.

morphs.name: Dampen Magic
morphs.note: Each piece of Light Armor worn increases damage absorbed. Increases shield cap value.
morphs.desc: Requires 5 pieces of light armor equipped Convert a portion of your Magicka into a protective ward, gaining a damage shield that absorbs 9297 damage for 6 seconds. Damage shield strength capped at 60% of your Max Health. Each piece of Light Armor worn increases the amount of damage absorbed by 6%.

morphs.name: Harness Magicka
morphs.note: Restores Magicka whenever you absorb damage.
morphs.desc: Requires 5 pieces of light armor equipped Convert a portion of your Magicka into a protective ward, gaining a damage shield that absorbs 9297 damage for 6 seconds. Damage shield strength capped at 50% of your Max Health. While active, whenever the shield absorbs damage, you restore 229 Magicka. Each piece of Light Armor worn increases the Magicka restored by 33%. This effect can occur up to 3 times.

athletics.name: Athletics
athletics.desc: Increases the Movement Speed bonus of Sprint by 2% for each piece of Medium Armor equipped. Reduces the cost of Roll Dodge by 2% for each piece of Medium Armor equipped.
athletics.desc_max: Increases the Movement Speed bonus of Sprint by 3% for each piece of Medium Armor equipped. Reduces the cost of Roll Dodge by 4% for each piece of Medium Armor equipped.

battlefield-mobility.name: Battlefield Mobility
battlefield-mobility.desc: WITH ONE HAND WEAPON AND SHIELD EQUIPPED Reduces the Movement Speed penalty of Bracing. Current penalty: 48%
battlefield-mobility.desc_max: WITH ONE HAND WEAPON AND SHIELD EQUIPPED Reduces the Movement Speed penalty of Bracing. Current penalty: 36%

absorb.name: Absorb
absorb.desc: WITH RESTORATION STAFF EQUIPPED Restores 300 Magicka whenever you block an attack. This effect can occur once every .25 seconds.
absorb.desc_max: WITH RESTORATION STAFF EQUIPPED Restores 600 Magicka whenever you block an attack. This effect can occur once every .25 seconds.

blessing-of-protection.name: Blessing of Protection
blessing-of-protection.desc: Slam your staff down to activate its blessings, healing you and your allies in front of you for 7146 Health. Also grants Minor Resolve, increasing you and your allies' Physical Resistance and Spell Resistance by 2974 for 10 seconds.

morphs.name: Blessing of Restoration
morphs.note: Increases the size, healing done, and duration.
morphs.desc:
Duration: 20 seconds.
Slam your staff down to activate its blessings, healing you and your allies in front of you for 8120 Health. Also grants Minor Resolve, increasing you and your allies' Physical Resistance and Spell Resistance by 2974 for 20 seconds.

morphs.name: Combat Prayer
morphs.note: Also grants Minor Berserk, increasing you and your allies' damage done. Cost decreases as ability ranks up.
morphs.desc:
Cost: 4590 Magicka.
Slam your staff down to activate its blessings, healing you and your allies in front of you for 7146 Health. Also grants Minor Berserk and Minor Resolve increasing you and your allies' damage done by 5% and Physical Resistance and Spell Resistance by 2974 for 10 seconds.

aspect-of-terror.name: Aspect of Terror
aspect-of-terror.desc:
Cost: 3780 Magicka.
Embody a dark spirit to terrify nearby enemies, causing them to cower in fear for 2 seconds and be afflicted with Major Cowardice for 10 seconds, reducing their Weapon and Spell Damage by 430.

morphs.name: Mass Hysteria
morphs.note: The ability no longer has a cap of how many targets it can affect and the fear increases in duration as the ability ranks up.
morphs.desc:
Duration: 3 seconds.
Embody a dark spirit to terrify all nearby enemies, causing them to cower in fear for 3 seconds and be afflicted with Major Cowardice for 10 seconds, reducing their Weapon and Spell Damage by 430.

morphs.name: Manifestation of Terror
morphs.note: Reduces the cost and creates a trap at your target location instead, which fears enemies when triggered.
morphs.desc:
Cost: 3240 Magicka, Duration: 20 seconds, Range: 22 meters, Target: Ground.
Conceal a sinister trap at the target location, which takes 2 seconds to arm and lasts for 20 seconds. When the trap is triggered, up to 6 enemies in the area become terrified, causing them to cower in fear for 2 seconds and be afflicted with Major Cowardice for 10 seconds, reducing their Weapon and Spell Damage by 430.

bolt-escape.name: Bolt Escape
bolt-escape.desc: Transform yourself into pure energy and flash forward, stunning enemies near your final location for 3 seconds. This effect cannot be blocked. Casting again within 4 seconds costs 33% more Magicka.

morphs.name: Streak
morphs.note: Now deals damage and stuns enemies between your beginning and final location.
morphs.desc:
Target: Self.
Transform yourself into pure energy and flash forward, dealing 3936 Shock Damage to enemies in your wake and stunning them for 3 seconds. This effect cannot be blocked. Casting again within 4 seconds costs 33% more Magicka.

morphs.name: Ball of Lightning
morphs.note: Summons a ball of lightning that protects you from projectiles, but no longer stuns enemies. Grants brief snare and immobilization immunity after casting.
morphs.desc: Transform yourself into pure energy and flash forward. After reaching your location, you become immune to snare and immobilize effects for 2 seconds. A ball of lightning is summoned at your end point, which intercepts up to 1 projectile attack made against you every 1 second for 3 seconds. Casting again within 4 seconds costs 33% more Magicka.

battle-resurrection.name: Battle Resurrection
battle-resurrection.desc: Reduces the time it takes you to resurrect another player by 15% while you are in a PvP area.
battle-resurrection.desc_max: Reduces the time it takes you to resurrect another player by 30% while you are in a PvP area.

barrier.name: Barrier
barrier.desc: Invoke defensive tactics to protect yourself and nearby group members with wards that each absorb up to 31764 damage for 30 seconds.

morphs.name: Reviving Barrier
morphs.note: Shielded targets heal over time.
morphs.desc: Invoke defensive tactics to protect yourself and nearby group members with wards that each absorb up to 31764 damage for 30 seconds. The wards also heal you and your group members for 14760 Health over 15 seconds.

morphs.name: Replenishing Barrier
morphs.note: Each time a ward dissolves you restore Magicka.
morphs.desc: Invoke defensive tactics to protect yourself and nearby group members with wards that each absorb up to 31764 damage. Each time a ward dissolves, you restore 1500 Magicka.

battle-rush.name: Battle Rush
battle-rush.desc: WITH TWO-HANDED WEAPON EQUIPPED Increases your Stamina Recovery by 15% for 10 seconds after killing a target.
battle-rush.desc_max: WITH TWO-HANDED WEAPON EQUIPPED Increases your Stamina Recovery by 30% for 10 seconds after killing a target.

blood-altar.name: Blood Altar
blood-altar.desc:
Duration: 30 seconds.
Sacrifice your life essence to conjure a fountain of blood to apply Minor Lifesteal to enemies in the area, healing you and your allies for 600 Health every 1 second when damaging them. Allies in the area can activate the Blood Funnel synergy, healing for 40% of their Max Health.

morphs.name: Sanguine Altar
morphs.note: Increases the duration and reduces the cost.
morphs.desc:
Cost: 2160 Health, Duration: 40 seconds.
Sacrifice your life essence to conjure a fountain of blood to apply Minor Lifesteal to enemies in the area, healing you and your allies for 600 Health every 1 second when damaging them. Allies in the area can activate the Blood Funnel synergy, healing for 40% of their Max Health.

morphs.name: Overflowing Altar
morphs.note: The synergy heals allies for more. Reduces the cost as the ability ranks up.
morphs.desc:
Cost: 4050 Health.
Sacrifice your life essence to conjure a fountain of blood to apply Minor Lifesteal to enemies in the area, healing you and your allies for 600 Health every 1 second when damaging them. Allies in the area can activate the Blood Feast synergy, healing for 65% of their Max Health.

blood-ritual.name: Blood Ritual
blood-ritual.desc: Allows you to infect another player with Noxiphilic Sanguivoria once every week by returning to the Vampire ritual site. Players already infected with Lycanthropy cannot be infected with Noxiphilic Sanguivoria.

blade-cloak.name: Blade Cloak
